family.ask: Ask: “What has been hard for us in the Fast so far? What can we start again?”

illus: An illustration

On a long pilgrimage walk from Thiruvananthapuram toward a shrine in the hills, a group of parishioners reached a roadside cross at midday. Someone had told them it marked the halfway point. Their feet were blistered and two of the younger men were talking about taking a bus. The old priest who walked with them asked them all to sit around the cross for a few minutes. He said: you have already done half. Look at him. He walked all the way to the end for you. They drank water, prayed one decade of the rosary, and stood up. Nobody took the bus.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, lifted up on the Cross, we look to you. Heal us and strengthen us for the rest of the Fast. Amen.
share: Everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). What wound do I need to bring before the Cross?
They shall look on the one whom they have pierced (Zechariah 12:10). Do I feel sorrow for my sins when I look at the crucifix?
Thus far the Lord has helped us (1 Samuel 7:12). How has God helped me in the first half of this Fast?
pm.resp: Lord, by your Cross, save us.
interc: For the whole Church at the middle of the Great Fast, that we may persevere.
For those who have given up their Lenten resolutions, that they may begin again.
For the sick and those who suffer, that they may find strength in the Cross.
For all who bear wounds of sin and addiction, that they may look to Christ and live.
For our parish, that the Cross in our midst may draw many to confession and the Holy Qurbono.
pm.close: Father, you so loved the world that you gave your only Son. As we look on him lifted up, pour out on us the spirit of compassion and supplication, keep us faithful through the testing, and bring us to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Sarah demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away; Abraham was distressed, and God promised to make a nation of the boy.
Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up; there is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ.
Jesus commands us to love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us, as the Father is generous to all.
2027-03-04.action: Pray today, by name, for someone who has hurt you.
2027-03-04.question: Whom am I keeping outside the tent of my love?

family.explain: Jesus says something very hard: love your enemies and pray for people who are mean to you. Why? Because God is like that. He lets the sun shine on good people and bad people. When we are kind to someone who is not kind to us, we are acting like God's children.
family.intention: We pray for someone who has been unkind to us.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we find hard to love? Can we pray for them together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in a village near Kottayam stopped speaking after their father's death, over a strip of rubber land on the boundary. For six years they passed each other at church without a word. During one Great Fast the younger brother's wife fell ill and was admitted to hospital. The older brother heard of it at the Wednesday prayer meeting. That evening he went to the hospital, sat outside the ward for a long time, and finally went in with a flask of kanji. He did not mention the land. Neither did his brother. The strip is still there, and so are the brothers, on speaking terms.

pm.open: Father in heaven, you love the good and the evil alike. Make our hearts like yours. Amen.
share: The matter was very distressing to Abraham on account of his son (Genesis 21:11). Where has jealousy or fear of loss caused pain in my family?
Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up (1 Corinthians 8:1). Do I use what I know to build others up or to feel superior?
Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). Whom is Jesus asking me to pray for today?
pm.resp: Lord, teach us to love as you love.
interc: For families divided by property disputes and inheritance.
For mothers and children who have been abandoned or sent away.
For our enemies and for those who persecute Christians.
For teachers and the learned, that their knowledge may serve love.
For the children of Abraham, Jews, Christians and Muslims, that they may live in peace.
pm.close: Father, you are perfect in love. Heal our divisions, turn our knowledge into service, and give us courage to love those who hate us, so that we may truly be your children. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In the wilderness God heard the voice of the boy Ishmael and opened Hagar's eyes to a well of water.
Paul says: keep alert, stand firm in faith, be courageous and strong; let all that you do be done in love.
Jesus, the Good Shepherd, knows his own, lays down his life, and gathers other sheep into one flock.
2027-03-05.action: Pray today for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and for your bishop.
2027-03-05.question: Where do I need God to open my eyes to a well I have not seen?

family.explain: Hagar and her little boy were alone in the desert with no water. The boy was crying, and Hagar was crying too. But God heard the boy crying, and God showed Hagar a well of water. God hears us too, wherever we are. Today we also pray for our Catholicos, the shepherd of our Church.
family.intention: We pray for children who are thirsty, hungry or alone, and for our Catholicos.
family.ask: Ask: “When did God help us when we felt alone?”

illus: An illustration

A young nurse from Mavelikara, newly arrived in a hospital in a northern European city, found herself on night duty in a ward where no one spoke Malayalam and she understood half of what was said. One night, after a patient died, she sat in the staff room and cried. A cleaner, an old woman from the Philippines, came in, said nothing, and put a cup of tea and a small holy card of the Good Shepherd beside her. The next Sunday the cleaner took her to a Mass where she found three other nurses from Kerala. She says: I was looking for a way home. God showed me the well that was already there.

pm.open: Lord, you hear us where we are. Open our eyes to see your gifts, and make us one flock under you, the Good Shepherd. Amen.
share: God has heard the voice of the boy where he is (Genesis 21:17). Do I believe God hears me even in my wilderness?
Let all that you do be done in love (1 Corinthians 16:14). Which of my daily tasks needs more love?
I know my own and my own know me (John 10:14). How well do I know the voice of the Good Shepherd?
pm.resp: Lord, hear us where we are.
interc: For Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis, our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, on the anniversary of his enthronement.
For mothers and children in deserts of poverty, war and exile.
For migrants and those working far from home.
For those who have drifted from the Church, the sheep outside the fold.
For unity among all Christians, one flock under one shepherd.
pm.close: Father, you heard Ishmael's cry and you sent your Son to gather all your scattered children. Bless the shepherds of your Church, open our eyes to your gifts, and keep us firm in faith and generous in love until Christ comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abraham and Abimelech made a covenant at Beer-sheba, and Abraham called on the name of the Everlasting God.
Everything created by God is good, received with thanksgiving and sanctified by God's word and prayer.
Jesus would not stay in one place: he was sent to proclaim the kingdom to other cities also.
2027-03-06.action: Settle one small quarrel peacefully this week.
2027-03-06.question: Why do I fast, and does my fasting make me more thankful and more generous?

family.explain: After healing many sick people, Jesus went to a quiet place to pray. The people wanted him to stay with them always. But Jesus said: I have to tell the good news about God to other towns too. That is why I was sent. Jesus wants everyone to hear about God's love.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for people who have never heard of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is someone we can tell about Jesus or invite to church?”

illus: An illustration

In a hamlet near Adoor two families quarrelled for years over a shared well on their boundary. One summer the well nearly dried up. The older of the two fathers, a quiet man who had just come back from a Lenten retreat, called a well-digger, paid to deepen it, and then put up a small board beside it with the names of both families. His wife asked why he put the neighbours' name first. He said: if the water is God's, the order does not matter. That Easter both families carried the same well water to bless their homes.

pm.open: Everlasting God, we call on your name. Make us peacemakers, thankful for your gifts, and send us out with your good news. Amen.
share: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the Lord (Genesis 21:33). What “tree of hope” am I planting for the future?
Everything created by God is good... received with thanksgiving (1 Timothy 4:4). Does my fasting make me more grateful?
I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also (Luke 4:43). Where is Jesus sending me?
pm.resp: Lord, send us out with your good news.
interc: For peace in disputes over water, land and resources.
For farmers and all who depend on rain and wells.
For missionaries and evangelizers, especially in North India.
For the poor who will share the fruits of our fasting.
For our parish as we prepare for K'piphtho Sunday.
pm.close: Father, you are the Everlasting God, faithful to your promises. Make us peacemakers, thankful stewards of your creation, and joyful messengers of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God tested Abraham, who answered, “Here I am,” and set out for Moriah with Isaac.
Isaac carried the wood; Abraham trusted that God himself would provide the lamb.
Jesus' disciples will fast when the Bridegroom is taken away; the new wine needs fresh wineskins.
2027-03-08.action: Begin tomorrow with the words: Here I am, Lord.
2027-03-08.question: What am I holding so tightly that I could not offer it to God?

family.explain: God asked Abraham to do something very hard. Abraham trusted God and set out with his son Isaac. Isaac carried the wood on his back, just as Jesus later carried his Cross. When Isaac asked where the lamb was, Abraham said: God himself will provide the lamb. God did provide, and for us he gave Jesus, the Lamb of God.
family.intention: We pray for families who are going through a hard test.
family.ask: Ask: “When was it hard for us to trust God, and how did he help us?”

illus: An illustration

A carpenter in Kottarakkara, a widower, took his teenage son along to every job during the boy's school holidays. One morning the boy, carrying the heaviest planks up a hill to a half-built house, asked why his father always gave him the wood and kept only the small bag of tools. His father laughed and said: because the tools are sharp, and I do not want you to get hurt. Years later, when the son was himself a father, he read Genesis 22 in church and stopped at the line where Isaac carries the wood and Abraham carries the fire and the knife. He told his wife that evening that he had finally understood his father.

pm.open: Lord, here we are. Teach us to trust you as Abraham trusted you. Amen.
share: Here I am (Genesis 22:1). Am I ready to say these words to God today?
God himself will provide the lamb (Genesis 22:8). Where do I need to trust that God will provide?
Then they will fast in those days (Luke 5:35). What does my fast this Lent say about my love for Jesus?
pm.resp: Lord, you will provide.
interc: For parents who carry heavy worries for their children.
For all who are being tested in faith, health or work.
For those who are fasting this Lent, that their fast may be full of love.
For our Church, that we may keep the traditions handed on to us with reverence and joy.
For all who will be baptised or return to the sacraments this Easter.
pm.close: Father, you gave your only Son as the Lamb for our sins. Make us obedient like Abraham, patient like Isaac, and faithful in our fast until the Bridegroom returns. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The angel stopped Abraham's hand; a ram was offered instead of Isaac, and the place was called “The Lord will provide.”
Jesus foretold his Passion and called all who follow him to deny themselves and take up their cross.
The Forty Martyrs of Sebaste chose a frozen lake over denying Christ.
2027-03-09.action: Accept one discomfort today in silence and offer it for someone who suffers.
2027-03-09.question: What is the warm bath-house on the shore that tempts me to leave Christ?

family.explain: Jesus says that to follow him we must carry our cross. Long ago forty soldiers at Sebaste stood all night on a frozen lake because they would not stop loving Jesus. One gave up, but a guard came and took his place. We can carry small crosses too: being kind when we are tired, sharing when we want to keep.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith today.
family.ask: Ask: “What small cross can each of us carry this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a hostel in Delhi a girl from Kollam was the only one on her floor who went to Holy Qurbono on Sunday mornings. The others slept late and teased her as she left in the cold. One January morning she nearly stayed in bed; the room was warm, the road outside was foggy, and no one would know. She went. Some weeks later a quiet girl from another state, who had never spoken to her, asked if she could come along. She said she had watched her go out every Sunday in the cold, and she wanted to see what was worth it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you gave yourself for us. Give us courage to take up our cross and follow you. Amen.
share: Now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son (Genesis 22:12). What am I holding back from God?
Let them deny themselves and take up their cross (Mark 8:34). Which cross am I trying to avoid?
I am completing what is lacking in Christ's afflictions (Colossians 1:24). How can my suffering become an offering for others?
pm.resp: Lord, strengthen us to follow you.
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith in our time.
For soldiers, police and all who serve in harsh conditions.
For those tempted to give up their faith for comfort or advancement.
For the sick, that they may unite their pain to the Cross of Christ.
For our parish, that we may persevere to the end of the Great Fast.
pm.close: Father, you did not withhold your only Son but gave him up for us all. By the prayers of the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste make us faithful to death, that we may receive the crown of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: News came to Abraham of his brother Nahor's family; Bethuel became the father of Rebekah.
Elders who rule well, especially in preaching and teaching, are worthy of double honour; choose them with care.
Jesus had compassion on the crowd and fed four thousand with seven loaves.
2027-03-10.action: Thank a priest and pray for him by name.
2027-03-10.question: Do I honour and pray for those who feed me with God's word?

family.explain: Jesus saw that the people were hungry and felt sorry for them. The disciples had only seven loaves and a few fish, but Jesus thanked God, broke the bread and gave it to the disciples to share. Everyone ate and there were seven baskets left over! Today Jesus still gives us the Bread of Life through our priests at the Holy Qurbono.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for all priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone who is hungry?”

illus: An illustration

In a high-range parish in Idukki, an old priest kept a jar of rice by the sacristy door. Anyone could take a measure, no questions asked, and anyone could add one. After his funeral the parishioners found a school notebook in his room. On every page he had written the names of families he had brought Holy Communion to in their homes, with small notes: knee pain, son abroad, waiting for rain. On the last page was a line he must have written for himself: they gave me the bread; I only carried it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have compassion on all who are hungry. Feed us with your word and your Body. Amen.
share: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah (Genesis 22:23). Where has God been quietly preparing something good in my family?
Let the elders who rule well be considered worthy of double honor (1 Timothy 5:17). How do I honour and support my priests?
I have compassion for the crowd (Matthew 15:32). Whose hunger have I noticed this week?
pm.resp: Lord, have compassion on us.
interc: For our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops and all priests.
For priests who are tired, sick or falsely accused.
For young men discerning a call to the priesthood.
For the hungry in our town and in the world.
For our families, that we may see God's hand in ordinary days.
pm.close: Father, your Son had compassion on the crowd and fed them in the desert. Bless the priests who break the bread of life for us, and make us generous in sharing our bread with others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Sarah died at Hebron; Abraham mourned and wept for her and, as a stranger, asked the Hittites for a burial place.
Paul thanks God for the Colossians' faith and love, born of the hope laid up for them in heaven.
Jesus refused to give a sign from heaven except the sign of Jonah.
2027-03-11.action: Pray for a departed member of your family by name.
2027-03-11.question: Do I live as a citizen of heaven or as if this world were my only home?

family.explain: When Sarah died, Abraham cried for her. He loved her very much. Even though God had promised him the land, Abraham did not yet own any of it, and he had to ask for a place to bury her. Abraham knew that his real home was with God. Jesus rose from the tomb on the third day, so we know that death is not the end.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom shall we remember in our prayers tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A Malayali nurse who had worked in the Gulf for twenty-eight years came home for her mother's funeral in Mavelikara. Her colleagues abroad had always called her the one from Kerala; in her own village the neighbours now called her the one from the Gulf. Standing by the grave after the prayers, she said to the priest that she did not belong anywhere any more. The old priest pointed to the cross on the tomb and said: neither did Abraham. That is why God gave him a city. She has kept the funeral card with that line written on the back.

pm.open: Lord, our true home is with you. Keep our hearts fixed on the hope you have prepared for us. Amen.
share: Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her (Genesis 23:2). Have I allowed myself to grieve with faith?
I am a stranger and an alien residing among you (Genesis 23:4). Where am I too attached to this world?
No sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah (Matthew 16:4). What signs do I demand from God?
pm.resp: Lord, you are our hope.
interc: For all who are mourning a husband, wife or parent.
For our departed relatives, friends and benefactors.
For migrants and those who live far from home.
For good relations between people of different faiths in our land.
For those who seek signs, that they may find the risen Christ.
pm.close: Father, you call us to be pilgrims on the earth and citizens of heaven. Comfort the grieving, receive our departed into your light, and let the sign of your Son's Resurrection keep our hope alive. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ephron offered the field as a gift; Abraham insisted on paying the full price of four hundred shekels.
Christ is our peace: by his blood those who were far off are brought near and made members of God's household.
Jesus warned against the yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod and asked: “Do you not yet understand?”
2027-03-12.action: Make peace with one person before Sunday.
2027-03-12.question: What wall have I built between myself and someone else?

family.explain: St Paul says that Jesus is our peace. He broke down the wall that kept people apart and made us all one family in God's house. Sometimes we build walls in our family when we are angry and do not speak to each other. Jesus helps us to break them down.
family.intention: We pray for families and neighbours who are quarrelling.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we need to make peace with this week?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in a village near Adoor had not spoken for eleven years because of a strip of land between their houses, less than two metres wide. A wall of hollow blocks stood on it. One Lent their mother, who was very ill, asked to be carried to the parish for the Way of the Cross. At the twelfth station she asked her sons to stand on either side of her. When she came home she said: I have one request before I die. Within a month the wall was down. The strip of land is now a path where their grandchildren run between the two houses.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are our peace. Break down the walls in our hearts and in our homes. Amen.
share: Abraham weighed out the silver… four hundred shekels (Genesis 23:16). Is there a debt or an unfair dealing I must set right?
He has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:14). Which wall must come down in my life?
Do you have eyes, and fail to see? (Mark 8:18). Where have I failed to see what Jesus has done for me?
pm.resp: Lord, you are our peace.
interc: For families divided by property disputes.
For peace between communities, castes and religions in our land.
For those who handle money, that they may be honest.
For hardened hearts, that Christ may soften them.
For all who walk the Way of the Cross today.
pm.close: Father, by the blood of your Son you made peace and gathered us into one household. Make us just in our dealings and reconciled with one another, so that we may celebrate Easter with one heart. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The field and cave of Machpelah became Abraham's possession, and there he buried Sarah in the land of promise.
Boasting is excluded: we are justified by faith, and the law is upheld, not overthrown.
Jesus calls us friends, chose us, and appointed us to bear fruit that will last.
2027-03-13.action: Do one hidden act of love for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-03-13.question: Do I live as one chosen and loved by Christ, or as one trying to earn his love?

family.explain: Jesus says: I do not call you servants, I call you friends. He chose each of us. The greatest love is to give your life for your friends, and that is what Jesus did on the Cross. Today we also pray for four of our bishops, whom Jesus chose to be shepherds of our Church.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and for all who serve the Church.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show Jesus' kind of love to someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolteacher in Thiruvalla kept a small card on her desk for thirty years. Her first headmistress had given it to her on her first day. It said only: you did not choose these children; they were given to you. On difficult days, when a class was noisy or a child seemed hopeless, she would turn the card over in her fingers. At her retirement a former student, now a doctor, stood up to speak and said: she treated each of us as if we had been chosen. Then he held up the same kind of card. She had given one to every student who had ever thanked her.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us your friends. Teach us to love one another as you have loved us. Amen.
share: Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah (Genesis 23:19). What does my faith say to me at the grave?
Then what becomes of boasting? It is excluded (Romans 3:27). Where do I still try to earn God's love?
You did not choose me but I chose you (John 15:16). How does it change me to know that Christ chose me?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your love.
interc: For Vincent Mar Paulos, Thomas Mar Antonios, Samuel Mar Irenios and Philipose Mar Stephanos, on the anniversary of their episcopal ordination.
For all bishops, that they may lay down their lives for their flocks.
For those who think they must earn God's love.
For friendships that are faithful and holy.
For our parish as we approach Samio Sunday and the last weeks of the Fast.
pm.close: Father, your Son called us friends and chose us to bear fruit that will last. Keep us humble in faith, generous in love, and faithful in hope until we see the city you have prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Old Abraham sends his servant to find a wife for Isaac, trusting God to send his angel ahead.
Paul, an ambassador in chains, asks for prayer at all times.
Jesus is asked by what authority he acts; his questioners will not answer the truth they fear.
2027-03-15.action: Give one worrying decision to God in prayer this morning.
2027-03-15.question: Do I come to Jesus to obey him, or to argue with him?

family.explain: Abraham was very old. He wanted a good wife for his son Isaac, so he sent his most trusted servant on a long journey. The servant was worried, but Abraham said: God will send his angel before you. Abraham could not see the future, but he knew God had always looked after him.
family.intention: We pray for young people who are choosing their path in life.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we are worried about, that we can give to God together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

An old man in Kottayam, a retired schoolteacher, kept a small diary of answered prayers. When his grandson was anxious about where to study, the old man did not give advice at first. He opened the diary and read out, year by year, the things he had once worried about and how God had carried the family through each one. Then he closed it and said: I do not know what will happen to you. I only know who has been faithful to us. The boy said later that this did more for him than any counsel.

pm.open: Lord God, you go before us. Make us alert and persevering in prayer, and teach us to trust you where we cannot see. Amen.
share: He will send his angel before you (Genesis 24:7). Where do I need to trust that God goes before me?
Pray in the Spirit at all times (Ephesians 6:18). How faithful is my daily prayer in these last days of the Fast?
They were afraid of the crowd (Mark 11:32). When has fear of others kept me from saying what I know is true?
pm.resp: Lord, go before us.
interc: For young people discerning marriage, priesthood or religious life.
For priests, catechists and missionaries, that they may proclaim the gospel boldly.
For Christians imprisoned for their faith, ambassadors in chains.
For the elderly, that they may hand on their faith with trust.
For all of us, that we may finish the Forty Days in faithful prayer.
pm.close: Father, you were faithful to Abraham in his old age and you hear the prayer of your Church. Go before us, keep us alert in prayer, and give us the courage to acknowledge the authority of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At the well, Abraham's servant prays for guidance and asks for a girl with a generous heart.
Paul rejoices to suffer for the Church, the Body of Christ; Christ in us is the hope of glory.
Jesus foretells his death and rising; the disciples do not understand and are afraid to ask.
2027-03-16.action: Pray one sentence before every important decision today.
2027-03-16.question: What question about the Cross have I been afraid to ask Jesus?

family.explain: Abraham's servant came to a well after a long journey. He did not rush. He made his camels kneel down and he prayed: Lord, help me today. He asked God to show him a kind girl, one who would give water not only to him but to all his camels too. God loves it when we pray before we do important things.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who has a big decision to make this week.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do tomorrow that is more than what we are asked?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Pathanamthitta there was an old woman who had been bedridden for eleven years. Beside her pillow she kept a list of names: the parish priest, the seminarians of the diocese, families in trouble. Every morning she said: Lord, today my pain is for these. When a new priest came to the parish, he was taken to see her on his first day. The old priests told him: this room is where the parish gets its strength. He did not believe it at first. After some years he said he did.

pm.open: Lord, we come to the well of your word. Hear us before we finish speaking, and let Christ dwell in us, our hope of glory. Amen.
share: O Lord, please grant me success today (Genesis 24:12). Do I pray before I act, or only after things go wrong?
I am completing what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions (Colossians 1:24). What suffering in my life could I offer for the Church?
They were afraid to ask him (Mark 9:32). What am I afraid to ask the Lord?
pm.resp: Lord, hear our prayer.
interc: For all who must make important decisions this week.
For the sick, the bedridden and those in chronic pain, that they may know their suffering is precious in the Body of Christ.
For persecuted Christians, in whom Christ still suffers.
For young people seeking a husband or wife, that they may look for a generous heart.
For all preparing to celebrate Holy Week.
pm.close: Father, your Son foretold his Passion and his Resurrection. Give us courage to ask, wisdom to pray before we choose, and grace to unite our sufferings with his. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Rebekah gives water to the servant and, unasked, to all his camels; the servant blesses God.
Be imitators of God and live in love, as Christ gave himself up for us.
Jesus reads in Nazareth: the Spirit has anointed him to bring good news to the poor and release to captives.
2027-03-17.action: Do one task today more fully and gladly than you were asked.
2027-03-17.question: Is my generosity measured, or does it go to the end?

family.explain: A young woman named Rebekah came to the well. A tired traveller asked her for a drink. She gave him water, and then she said: I will give water to your camels too! She ran back and forth again and again until all ten camels had enough. God was pleased with her kind heart. Today is also the day of St Patrick, who brought Jesus to Ireland.
family.intention: We pray for the people of Ireland and for all missionaries.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we help tomorrow, even if they do not ask us?”

illus: An illustration

Every summer, outside a small shop near the bus stand in Adoor, an old man sets up a water booth, a thanneer panthal: a clay pot, a few steel tumblers, sometimes buttermilk with ginger and curry leaves. He does not ask who you are or what you believe. Drivers, schoolchildren and labourers stop to drink. When asked why he does it, he said: when I was a boy I walked to school in the heat and a woman gave me water every day. I never knew her name. This is my way of paying her back.

pm.open: Lord, you hear us before we finish speaking. Make us imitators of you, as beloved children, and fill us with your Spirit to bring good news. Amen.
share: I will draw for your camels also (Genesis 24:19). Where can I give more than I am asked?
Live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us (Ephesians 5:2). What does it mean for me to give myself, not only my things?
He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives (Luke 4:18). Who around me is a captive, to fear, addiction or loneliness?
pm.resp: Lord, make us imitators of you.
interc: For the Church in Ireland, and for all Irish missionaries who served in India.
For people in slavery and trafficking today, that they may be set free.
For all who serve strangers with no hope of return.
For missionaries who have returned to difficult places to preach the gospel.
For the grace to love and pray for those who have hurt us.
pm.close: Father, St Patrick returned to the land of his captivity with the good news of your Son. By his prayers make us generous like Rebekah, loving like Christ, and bold to bring release to captives. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abraham's servant will not eat until he has told his errand; he speaks only of his master.
Clothe yourselves with love and let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.
You are the salt of the earth and the light of the world.
2027-03-18.action: Read one Gospel chapter slowly today and share one verse at supper.
2027-03-18.question: When I speak of my faith, do I speak more of myself or of the Lord?

family.explain: Jesus says we are like salt that makes food tasty, and like a lamp that lights up the whole house. When we are kind, honest and joyful, people around us can see God's love. Today we remember St Cyril, a bishop in Jerusalem who loved teaching people about Jesus, especially about Jesus really present in the Holy Qurbono.
family.intention: We pray for our Sunday school teachers and for our archbishop.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us be a little light in our home this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a Malankara parish near Mavelikkara, a Sunday school teacher retired after forty-one years. At the farewell, one former pupil after another came up to speak: a doctor, a bus conductor, two priests, a mother of five. None of them remembered much of the syllabus. All of them remembered the same thing: every Sunday, before the lesson, she would point to the tabernacle and say, children, Jesus is really here, so speak softly. A priest said: I learned the doctrine of the Eucharist in the seminary. I learned to believe it in her class.

pm.open: Lord, let the word of Christ dwell in us richly. Make us faithful messengers, salt and light in the world. Amen.
share: I will not eat until I have told my errand (Genesis 24:33). What comes first in my day: my comfort or the Lord's work?
Above all, clothe yourselves with love (Colossians 3:14). Which virtue on Paul's list do I most need to put on?
Let your light shine before others (Matthew 5:16). Where has my light been hidden under a basket?
pm.resp: Lord, make us salt and light.
interc: For Archbishop Thomas Mar Koorilos on his name day, and for all our bishops.
For catechists, Sunday school teachers and parents, who hand on the faith.
For all preparing for baptism or reception into the Church this Easter.
For deeper faith in the real presence of Christ in the Holy Qurbono.
For the Church in Jerusalem and for peace in the Holy Land.
pm.close: Father, Mar Cyril taught your people beside the Tomb of your Son. By his prayers let your word dwell in us richly, deepen our faith in the holy mysteries, and make our lives shine before others, that they may glorify you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The forty days are complete: Jesus conquers with the word of God the tempter who overcame Adam.
The fast God chooses is mercy, amendment of life, and an offering that costs; we were ransomed by the precious blood of Christ.
St Joseph, a righteous man, did at once what the angel of the Lord commanded.
2027-03-19.action: Give today what you saved by fasting during these forty days.
2027-03-19.question: Where did I fall in these forty days, and where did the word of God help me stand?
2027-03-19.special: The Fortieth Friday and the feast of Mar Yauseph (St Joseph): no fasting and no forty prostrations today (Panchangam). Announce Lazarus Saturday (20 Mar) and Hosanna Sunday (21 Mar); remind the faithful to bring palm leaves and flowers.

family.explain: Today the forty days of the Great Fast are finished. Jesus fasted forty days, and when the devil tempted him, Jesus answered with words from the Bible. Today is also the feast of St Joseph. When the angel told Joseph what to do, he got up and did it at once. Jesus and Joseph both listened to God's word.
family.intention: We pray for all fathers, and for families that are struggling.
family.ask: Ask: “What did our family give up or do in these forty days, and what did we learn?”

illus: An illustration

A rubber tapper near Ranni rose at four every morning for thirty-eight years. He spoke little. When his wife fell ill he took over the cooking without a complaint; when his son failed an examination he said only, we will try again. At his funeral the parish priest asked the children what they remembered most. The eldest daughter said: I never once heard him raise his voice, and I never once saw him miss his evening prayer. The priest said: then you have seen something of St Joseph.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you fasted forty days and overcame the tempter by the word of God. Thank you for these forty days. With Mar Yauseph, teach us to hear and obey. Amen.
share: The tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes (Genesis 3:6). Which of the three hungers most often tempts me: comfort, display or power?
Is not this the fast that I choose: to share your bread with the hungry? (Isaiah 58:6–7). Has my fast reached the poor?
He did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). What is God asking me to do now, without delay?
pm.resp: Lord, lead us not into temptation.
interc: In thanksgiving for the forty days of the Great Fast, and for all who kept it faithfully.
For fathers and foster fathers, for carpenters and all who work with their hands, through the prayers of St Joseph.
For all who are tempted to despair, addiction or dishonesty, that they may stand firm by the word of God.
For the hungry and the homeless, that our fasting may become their bread.
For our parishes as we prepare for Lazarus Saturday, Hosanna Sunday and the Week of the Passion.
pm.close: Father, your Son conquered the tempter in the wilderness, and Joseph, the righteous man, obeyed your word in silence. Let our forty days bear fruit in mercy and obedience, and bring us with your Son through his Passion to the joy of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus weeps at the tomb of Lazarus and raises him with a loud cry: “Lazarus, come out!”
Christ is the first fruits of those who have died; the last enemy, death, will be destroyed.
Rebekah answers, “I will,” and goes to meet her bridegroom; tomorrow we go with Christ to Jerusalem.
2027-03-20.action: Plan your Confession for this coming week.
2027-03-20.question: What tomb is the Lord calling me out of, and what binds me still?
2027-03-20.special: Lazarus Saturday. Tomorrow Hosanna Sunday (21 Mar): bring palm leaves and flowers; the Week of the Passion (Hasho) begins in the evening.

family.explain: Jesus' friend Lazarus died. His sisters Martha and Mary were very sad. When Jesus saw Mary crying, he cried too. Then he went to the tomb and called out loudly: Lazarus, come out! And Lazarus walked out alive. Jesus loves us so much that he cries with us when we are sad, and he is stronger than death. Tomorrow is Hosanna Sunday, when we wave palm leaves for Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the members of our family who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we miss who has died? Let us say their names and pray for them.”

illus: An illustration

A man from Kollam had not been to Confession for twenty-two years. Each Lent his wife asked him; each Lent he said, next year. One Lazarus Saturday he went with her to church only to help carry the palms for the next day. While he was stacking them, the priest was hearing confessions at the side of the church, and the line was short. He said afterwards that he stood there for ten minutes, holding a bundle of palm leaves, arguing with himself. Then he put them down and joined the line. When he came out, his wife saw his face and did not need to ask. He said only: I feel as if someone has untied my hands.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the resurrection and the life. Call us out of our tombs, unbind us, and make us ready to go with you into Jerusalem. Amen.
share: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (John 11:32). Have I ever blamed God for a loss? Can I bring that to Jesus now?
Jesus began to weep (John 11:35). Do I believe that Jesus shares my grief?
Unbind him, and let him go (John 11:44). What still binds me, and when will I bring it to Confession?
pm.resp: Lord, you are the resurrection and the life.
interc: For the faithful departed, especially those who have died in our families and parish this year.
For all who grieve, that they may know Jesus weeps with them.
For those far from the sacraments, that they may come out of the tomb and be unbound in Confession this Holy Week.
For the sick and the dying, that they may hope in the resurrection of the body.
For our parish as we prepare to welcome the Lord tomorrow with palms and Hosanna.
pm.close: Father, your Son wept at the grave of his friend and called him back to life. Strengthen our faith in the resurrection, set us free from what binds us, and make us ready to welcome him tomorrow and follow him through his Passion to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God offered his people rest, but their leaders would not hear.
The heavens wear out like clothing; the Lord remains the same.
In the temple Jesus was asked: by what authority? His answer would be the Cross.
2027-03-22.action: Do one hidden act of service today for someone who is tired.
2027-03-22.question: Where do I say “I do not know” to avoid what God is asking?

family.explain: This week is Hasha Week, the week when Jesus suffered and died for us. In the temple some leaders asked Jesus who gave him the right to do what he did. Jesus knew they were not really looking for the truth. Jesus is God's Son; everything belongs to him. This week he will show his power by loving us all the way to the Cross.
family.intention: We pray that our family will keep this holy week with Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family do each evening this week to stay close to Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Mavelikara the sacristan, an old man, used to put the same faded purple cloth on the lectern every Hasha Week. One year the youth group bought a new one and asked him to throw the old cloth away. He held it up to the light. It was thin, mended in three places. He said: this cloth has worn out serving the word. The word has not worn out at all. Put the new one on, but let me keep this one. They let him keep it, and on Good Friday he knelt on it at the back of the church.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in this week of your Passion we come to stay with you. Open our ears to your word. Amen.
share: This is rest; give rest to the weary... yet they would not hear (Isaiah 28:12). Where have I refused to hear God?
They will perish, but you remain (Hebrews 1:11). What in my life is wearing out, and what remains?
By what authority are you doing these things? (Matthew 21:23). Do I let Jesus have authority over my week?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us.
interc: For our Church as it enters Hasha Week, that we may keep these days with prayer and fasting.
For all who will come to confession this week, and for the priests who will hear them.
For people who are worn out by work, illness or grief, that someone may give them rest.
For leaders in Church and society, that they may seek truth and not their own safety.
For the soul of Fr Seraphion Attupurathu and for all who came into Catholic communion in the reunion of 1930.
pm.close: Father, your Son did not answer with force but with the gift of his life. Keep us beside him through this week, give rest to the weary through our hands, and bring us with joy to the day of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Before his death Moses commissioned Joshua: be strong and bold; I will be with you.
The promise of entering God's rest is still open to those who believe.
Jesus, troubled in soul, chose his hour; lifted up, he draws all people to himself.
2027-03-23.action: Offer peace today to someone you have quarrelled with.
2027-03-23.question: When I am troubled, do I run from my hour or give it to the Father?

family.explain: Jesus knew he was going to suffer. He said his heart was troubled. Jesus was not pretending; he really felt afraid, like we sometimes do. But he trusted his Father and did not run away. He said that when he was lifted up on the Cross he would draw everyone to himself, like a big hug for the whole world.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is afraid tonight.
family.ask: Ask: “When you are afraid, what can you say to God, as Jesus did?”

illus: An illustration

A retired headmaster in Kottayam kept, for forty years, a small black notebook in which he wrote one sentence about every child who left his school. When he was dying, he called the young teacher who would take over the school archive and gave her the notebook. She asked what she should do with it. He said: read one page a day and pray for that child, wherever he or she is now. I cannot go with them any more. You will. She told the story at his funeral, holding the notebook, and said she was on page eleven.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in your hour your soul was troubled. We bring you our fears tonight. Amen.
share: Your time to die is near; call Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:14). What has someone handed on to me that I must carry forward?
While the promise of entering his rest is still open (Hebrews 4:1). Am I living as if God's rest is my goal?
Now my soul is troubled... Father, glorify your name (John 12:27–28). What fear can I give to the Father tonight?
pm.resp: Lord, draw us to yourself.
interc: For all who are facing death or serious illness this week, that they may know the Lord is with them.
For those handing on responsibility in families, parishes and workplaces, and for those receiving it.
For all who are afraid of what is coming, that their fear may become trust.
For people of every nation, that the Lord lifted up on the Cross may draw them to himself.
For our Church in Hasha Week, that we may walk in the light while we have it.
pm.close: Father, your Son was lifted up so that he might draw all people to himself. Give us courage in our hour, keep us faithful to the end, and lead us with him into your rest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Judas, one of the twelve, sold Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
Ezekiel's sword of judgment is told: return to your sheath; Jesus takes the cup instead.
Christ was offered once for all to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself.
2027-03-24.action: Go to confession today if you have not yet done so this Lent.
2027-03-24.question: For what do I put Jesus second when following him costs me?

family.explain: Judas was one of Jesus' twelve friends, but he agreed to hand Jesus over for thirty silver coins. That was a very small price for the Son of God! Peter also let Jesus down later, but Peter cried and came back to Jesus, and Jesus forgave him. Whatever we do wrong, we can always come back to Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who has turned away from Jesus, that they may come back.
family.ask: Ask: “What will we do tomorrow, on Pesaha, to remember Jesus' Last Supper?”

illus: An illustration

A goldsmith in Thrissur was offered a large sum by a customer to stamp a higher purity mark on jewellery than it really had. Business was poor and his daughter's college fees were due. He asked for a day to think. That evening he sat in the parish church through the Hasha Wednesday prayers and heard the words: what will you give me? The next morning he told the customer no. He lost the order and, for a while, some other customers. Years later, when people ask why his shop is trusted, his daughter, now running it, tells them about one Wednesday evening.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were sold for thirty pieces of silver. We come tonight to choose you again. Amen.
share: Return it to its sheath! (Ezekiel 21:30). What sword, in word or in thought, do I need to put away?
He has appeared once for all... to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself (Hebrews 9:26). Do I trust that his one sacrifice is enough for my sins?
What will you give me if I betray him to you? (Matthew 26:15). What am I tempted to take in exchange for Jesus?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us, and keep us faithful.
interc: For all who have turned away from Christ, that they may come back with the tears of Peter.
For those who are tempted to sell their honesty or their faith for money or approval.
For the priests who tomorrow will celebrate Pesaha and wash the feet of their people.
For peace among nations, that every sword may be returned to its sheath.
For our families as they prepare the Pesaha table, that it may be a table of reconciliation.
pm.close: Father, your Son was offered once for all to take away the sins of many. Keep us from betraying him, raise us when we fall, and bring us tomorrow to his table with grateful hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The guards were paid to say that the body had been stolen; the tomb was empty because Christ was raised.
Through the body of Christ we died to the old life so that we may belong to the risen Lord.
We serve in the new life of the Spirit and bear fruit for God.
2027-03-29.action: Greet someone today with “Christ is risen!”
2027-03-29.question: To whom do I belong this Easter: to my old habits, or to the risen Lord?

family.explain: On Easter morning the soldiers who guarded Jesus' tomb saw that it was empty. Some leaders paid them money to tell a false story: that Jesus' friends had stolen his body while the soldiers slept. But the truth cannot be hidden. Jesus really rose from the dead, and soon many people saw him alive.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who does not yet know that Jesus is alive.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we tell someone this week that Jesus is risen?”

illus: An illustration

In a hospital in Thiruvalla a night nurse was told by a senior colleague to change the time written on a chart so that a delay in treatment would not be noticed. The patient had recovered; no one would ever know. It was Easter Monday. She had been to the Easter Qurbono only the night before, and she remembered the soldiers who were paid to change their story. She wrote the true time and reported the delay. She was not thanked for it that week. Some months later the hospital changed its night procedures, and the colleague, to her surprise, came to thank her.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, we rejoice in your Resurrection. Fill this gathering with your Easter joy. Amen.
share: You have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another (Romans 7:4). What does it mean for me to belong to the risen Lord?
Slaves not under the old written code but in the new life of the Spirit (Romans 7:6). What is new in my life this Easter?
So they took the money and did as they were directed (Matthew 28:15). Where am I tempted to keep silent about the truth?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, make us your witnesses.
interc: For the Church throughout the world in this Easter week, that her joy may reach those who are sad.
For all who were baptized or received into full communion this Easter.
For those who are paid or pressured to hide the truth, that they may have courage.
For the sick and elderly who could not come to the Easter services.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, and for friendship between Christians and Jews.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son from the dead, and no power could keep him in the tomb. Make us his own, let our lives bear fruit for you, and send us to tell the truth of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ our paschal lamb has been sacrificed; let us keep the feast with sincerity and truth.
A little yeast leavens the whole batch: clear out the old yeast of malice.
A lamp is put on the lampstand; the measure you give will be the measure you get.
2027-03-30.action: Give up one resentment today as your Easter offering.
2027-03-30.question: Is my Easter light on the lampstand, or under the bed?

family.explain: Jesus asks: would you light a lamp and then hide it under your bed? Of course not! You put it up high so that everyone can see. Jesus is risen, and he has put his light in our hearts. We should not hide it. We let it shine by being kind, honest and joyful.
family.intention: We pray that our family may shine with Jesus' Easter light.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way each of us can let Jesus' light shine tomorrow?”

illus: An illustration

A family in Pathanamthitta used to make their Pesaha bread from a recipe written in a grandmother's hand. One year the mother found, folded inside the recipe card, a second note in the same hand: before you make this bread, make peace with anyone you are angry with; the bread will taste better. The family laughed, then went quiet. That Easter week the mother finally rang her brother, to whom she had not spoken in three years over a land dispute. They did not settle the land that day. But he came to their house on New Sunday, and the children met their cousins for the first time.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, our paschal Lamb, we gather in your light. Clear our hearts and make us new. Amen.
share: Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch (1 Corinthians 5:7). What old yeast do I need to clear out?
Let us celebrate the festival... with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth (1 Corinthians 5:8). Is my life sincere and truthful?
Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket? (Mark 4:21). Where am I hiding my faith?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, let your light shine in us.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the festival of Easter with sincerity and truth.
For families divided by old quarrels, that this Easter may bring reconciliation.
For all who will receive the Holy Qurbono this week, that they may receive the Lamb with clean hearts.
For those who are ashamed of their faith, that they may set their light on the lampstand.
For the newly baptized, that their Easter light may never be hidden.
pm.close: Father, you gave us your Son as our paschal Lamb and raised him in glory. Make us a new batch, free of malice, and let the light of his Resurrection shine through us for all to see. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul charges Timothy: fight the good fight with faith and a good conscience.
Jesus looked at the rich man and loved him, and invited him to give all and follow.
For mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible.
2027-03-31.action: Give something you value to someone poor today.
2027-03-31.question: What is the one thing I still lack in following Jesus?

family.explain: A man ran to Jesus and asked how to live forever with God. Jesus looked at him with love and said: give what you have to the poor and come, follow me. But the man was sad, because he had many things and did not want to let them go. Jesus loves us too, and he asks us to love him more than any of our things.
family.intention: We pray for people who have very little, and for hearts that like to share.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing each of us could share with someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Kollam, home for Easter, had saved for a year to buy a new phone. At the Easter Qurbono he heard the parish appeal for a family whose house had burned in the summer. On Wednesday of that week he went back to the shop, cancelled the order and took the money to the parish office in an envelope without a name. He told no one. Months later his mother found the receipt from the cancelled order in his old jacket and asked what had happened. He said only: Jesus looked at me, and I could not walk away this time.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you look on us with love. Give us hearts free enough to follow you. Amen.
share: Fight the good fight, having faith and a good conscience (1 Timothy 1:18–19). What is my good fight this Easter?
Jesus, looking at him, loved him (Mark 10:21). Do I believe that Jesus looks at me with love?
For God all things are possible (Mark 10:27). What impossible thing do I need to entrust to God?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, set our hearts free.
interc: For all who are held captive by money or possessions, that they may find the freedom of the Gospel.
For the poor, and for those who share with them in this Easter season.
For those whose faith has suffered shipwreck, that the Lord may bring them safely back.
For young people discerning how to follow Jesus, that they may not walk away from his call.
For our parish, that the joy of Easter may become generosity.
pm.close: Father, for you all things are possible: you raised your Son from the dead. Raise us from every grip that holds us, keep our faith and conscience whole, and let us follow Jesus with joy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today Jesus sees a woman in the synagogue who has been bent over for eighteen years. For eighteen years she has looked only at the ground. Jesus calls her and says: “Woman, you are set free from your ailment.” He lays his hands on her, and immediately she stands up straight and praises God.

The leader of the synagogue is angry: healing is work, and the sabbath is for rest. Jesus replies: you untie your ox and your donkey on the sabbath to lead them to water. Should not this daughter of Abraham, bound for eighteen years, be set free on the sabbath? God's day is the day of freedom.

Many of us are bent in some way: by guilt, by worry, by an addiction, by grief, by carrying everything alone. We get used to looking at the ground. In this Fast Jesus calls us by name, lays his hands on us in Confession and in the Holy Qurbono, and says: stand up, look up, you are free.

And the evening Gospel tells us what to do once we are healed. The Good Samaritan saw a wounded man, was moved with pity, and bound up his wounds. Jesus says: “Go and do likewise.” This week, stop for someone you would usually pass by. Let us be healed, and become healers. Amen.
kids: Children, try bending over and looking only at the floor. Not nice, is it? A woman in the Bible had to walk like that for eighteen years!
Jesus saw her, called her, and touched her. And she stood up straight and praised God!
Jesus also told a story about a man who stopped to help someone hurt on the road. Let's help others too. Let's say: “Jesus, help me to help others!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the last Sunday before Holy Week we hear of two blind men who receive their sight. In John's Gospel a man blind from birth; in Mark's, Bartimaeus, a beggar sitting by the road at Jericho.

Jesus makes clay, anoints the blind man's eyes and sends him to wash in the pool of Siloam, which means “Sent”. He comes back seeing. Then come the questions, the arguments, the threats. He does not know how to answer the scholars, but he knows one thing: “I was blind; now I see.” And his faith grows until he kneels and says: “Lord, I believe.” Meanwhile those who are sure they see refuse the light.

Bartimaeus cannot see, but he can shout. “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” People tell him to be quiet. He shouts louder. Jesus stops and asks: “What do you want me to do for you?” “Teacher, let me see again.” He receives his sight and follows Jesus on the road, the road to Jerusalem.

Next Sunday is Hosanna. Holy Week begins. Let us ask Jesus to heal our blindness: to the poor beside us, to our own sins, to God's love. Let us pray Bartimaeus' prayer all through this week. And having received our sight, let us follow Jesus on the way, to his Cross and his Resurrection. Amen.
kids: Children, close your eyes for a moment. Now open them! It's wonderful to see, isn't it? Bartimaeus was blind. He heard Jesus was passing and shouted: “Jesus, help me!”
People said, “Be quiet!” But he shouted even louder. Jesus asked: “What do you want?” “I want to see!” And Jesus gave him his sight!
Next week we will wave palms for Jesus. Let's say: “Jesus, open my eyes to see you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we carry palms like the crowds of Jerusalem. Jesus rides into the holy city, and the people go out to meet him shouting: “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!” The prophet Zechariah had said: your King comes to you, humble, riding on a donkey.

Notice how he comes. Not on a war horse, like a conqueror, but on a donkey, the animal of ordinary people and of peace. He is a King, but his throne will be a cross and his crown will be thorns. When the Pharisees want the crowd silenced, Jesus says: “If these were silent, the stones would shout out.” All creation knows its King.

But the same city that cries “Hosanna” today will cry “Crucify him” on Friday. How quickly hearts change. And our hearts too: we praise him on Sunday and forget him on Monday. Holy Week is the time to ask for faithful hearts, hearts that keep shouting Hosanna even at the foot of the Cross.

Hosanna means “Save us, we pray.” Let us take our palms home not as decorations but as a promise: Lord, you are my King; save me. Come to all the services of this Holy Week. Walk with Jesus from the upper room to Calvary, and on to the empty tomb. Hosanna in the highest! Amen.
kids: Children, today we wave our palms like the children of Jerusalem! Jesus came riding on a little donkey, and everyone shouted: “Hosanna! Hosanna!”
Jesus is a King, but a gentle King of peace. This week we will remember how much he loved us: he gave his life on the cross, and then he rose again!
Take your palm home and put it near the cross. Let's shout together: “Hosanna to Jesus our King!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, tonight we enter the upper room. Jesus says: “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.” He knew what was coming: betrayal, arrest, the Cross. And on that night he gave us his greatest gift.

“He took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, saying: This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” And the cup: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood.” The lamb of the first Passover saved Israel from death; Jesus, the true Lamb, gives himself to save the whole world. Every Holy Qurbono since that night is this same gift.

And at the same table Jesus taught them how to be great: “I am among you as one who serves.” He knelt and washed their feet. We cannot receive the Body of Christ and refuse to serve the body of Christ in our brothers and sisters. The altar and the towel belong together.

Tonight, at home, families will break the Pesaha appam. Let it be a real family communion: forgive one another, remember those far away, thank God for the Qurbono and for our priests. And after supper, do not leave Jesus alone. Stay with him, as he goes out to pray in Gethsemane. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight is Pesaha. The night before Jesus died, he had a special supper with his friends. He took bread and said: “This is my body.” He took the cup and said: “This is my blood.” That was the first Holy Qurbana!
Then Jesus knelt down and washed his friends' feet, like a servant. He wanted to teach them to love and help one another.
Tonight at home, help someone without being asked. Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for giving us yourself!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we stand at the foot of the Cross. The One who was welcomed with Hosanna on Sunday is today mocked, scourged, crowned with thorns and nailed to a cross between two criminals. Isaiah had seen it: “He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; by his bruises we are healed.”

Listen to his words from the Cross. “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.” He forgives those who are killing him. To the thief who asks to be remembered, he promises: “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” To his Mother and the beloved disciple he says: “Here is your son; here is your mother.” He gives us his own Mother.

And then: “It is finished.” Not “I am finished”, but “It is accomplished.” The work of salvation is complete. The soldier's spear opens his side, and blood and water flow: the Fathers saw there the Eucharist and Baptism, the Church born from the heart of Christ.

Today there is no Qurbono; the altar is bare. We kneel before the Cross, we fast, we keep silence, and we stand with Mary who did not run away. Let each of us forgive someone today, as he forgave. We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Good Friday. Jesus died on the cross. He let it happen because he loves us so much and wanted to take away our sins.
On the cross Jesus forgave the people who hurt him. He told a thief who was sorry: “Today you will be with me in heaven.”
Today let's be quiet, pray, and say sorry to anyone we have hurt. Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for loving me so much!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is the day of the great silence. The Lord's body lies in the tomb. The disciples hide in fear. The stone is sealed and soldiers stand guard. It seems that death has won.

But the ancient Church sang a different song. While his body rested, Christ descended to the dead, to Adam and Eve, to Abraham and the prophets, to all who had waited for him. An old homily imagines him taking Adam by the hand: “Awake, O sleeper, and arise from the dead.” Holy Saturday is not empty; it is the hidden victory.

St Paul tells us that in Baptism we were buried with Christ, so that we might rise with him. Today is a good day to bury with him whatever is dead in us: a sin we keep returning to, a grudge, a fear. Bring it to the tomb, and leave it there.

And let us stay with Mary. On this day, when everyone else despaired, she kept faith. Let us keep silence, prepare our hearts and our homes, and wait for the night when the stone will be rolled away. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus' body is resting in the tomb. A big stone is in front, and soldiers are guarding it. Everyone is quiet and sad.
But Mary, Jesus' mother, kept trusting God. And tonight something wonderful will happen!
Today let's be quiet and get ready for Easter. Let's say: “Jesus, I'm waiting for you!”

homily: Christ is risen! He is risen indeed! Dear brothers and sisters, very early this morning the women went to the tomb with spices, expecting to anoint a dead body. Instead they found an angel who said: “Do not be afraid. He is not here; for he has been raised, as he said.”

As he said. On the road to Jerusalem Jesus had told his disciples three times that he would suffer, die and rise on the third day. They did not understand. Today God has kept his word. And Jesus himself meets the women: “Greetings!” They hold his feet and worship him. Peter and John run to the tomb; the beloved disciple “saw and believed”.

St Paul gives us the heart of the Gospel: “Christ died for our sins, he was buried, and he was raised on the third day.” Because Christ is risen, our sins can be forgiven; because Christ is risen, death is not the end; because Christ is risen, the graves of our loved ones are not the last word. Daniel came out of the lions' den at dawn; Christ came out of the tomb, and he will bring us out too.

St Peter said: “God raised this Jesus, and we are all witnesses.” Now we are the witnesses. Let us live as Easter people: joyful, forgiving, hopeful. Bring this joy to someone who is sad this week. Christ is risen! He is truly risen! Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Say it with me: He is risen indeed!
On Sunday morning the women went to Jesus' tomb and found it empty. An angel said: “He is not here, he is risen!” Then Jesus himself came to meet them. They were so happy!
Jesus is alive for ever, and he is with us. Today tell everyone at home: “Jesus is alive!” Let's shout: “Alleluia!”

homily: Dear friends, Abraham had wronged King Abimelech out of fear. He said: I thought, there is no fear of God at all in this place (Genesis 20:11). But the king was more honest than Abraham expected.
What does Abraham do then? He prays for the man he wronged: Abraham prayed to God; and God healed Abimelech (Genesis 20:17). This is a good Lenten practice: to pray for those we have hurt.

In the Gospel the disciples are in the storm, and Jesus comes walking on the sea: take heart, it is I; do not be afraid (Matthew 14:27). Peter walks to him, but when he notices the strong wind he begins to sink and cries out: Lord, save me! Jesus immediately reached out his hand and caught him (Matthew 14:30–31).

We are in the middle of the Great Fast. If you feel the wind more than before, look at Jesus, not at the waves, and say Peter's prayer. May the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways (2 Thessalonians 3:16). Amen.
kids: Children, Peter walked on the water to Jesus! But when he looked at the big waves he got scared and started to sink. He shouted: Lord, save me! And Jesus caught his hand at once. When you are scared, you can say the same short prayer: Jesus, save me. He always hears.

homily: Dear friends, the Lord did for Sarah as he had promised. Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age (Genesis 21:1–2). After long years of waiting, God kept his word.
Sarah once laughed in disbelief; now she says: God has brought laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me (Genesis 21:6). The Fast prepares us for the laughter of Easter.

Paul says we are all children of God through faith: as many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ; you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise (Galatians 3:26–29).
But Jesus warns the towns that saw his miracles and did not repent: woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! (Matthew 11:21). We have received so much grace. In this Fast, let it change us. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham and Sarah waited a very long time for a baby, and God gave them Isaac. His name means “he laughs,” because they were so happy! When you were baptized, God made you his child too. That is a reason to be happy every day.

homily: Dear friends, today we are halfway through the Great Fast, and the Church lifts up the Cross. The Panchangam calls this day the setting up of Golgotha. It is a signpost for tired travellers: this is where we are going, and this is what gives us strength.

In the desert the people became impatient on the way, and serpents bit them. God told Moses: make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). The cure was simply to look, in faith.

Jesus says: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life. For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3:14–16). Zechariah adds: they shall look on the one whom they have pierced, and mourn (Zechariah 12:10).

Paul encourages us: God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength (1 Corinthians 10:13). Let us say with Samuel: thus far the Lord has helped us (1 Samuel 7:12). Look at the Cross, taste the Lord's goodness at the altar, and walk on to Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, today is the middle of the Great Fast! The Church puts up a big Cross for us to see. Long ago, God told Moses to lift up a bronze snake, and everyone who looked at it got better. Jesus was lifted up on the Cross so that everyone who looks at him with love can be healed from sin. Look at the Cross today and say: thank you, Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, in the first reading a family is torn apart. Sarah says: cast out this slave woman with her son. The matter was very distressing to Abraham on account of his son (Genesis 21:10–11). Jealousy and fear of losing an inheritance still divide many families.
But God does not forget Ishmael: as for the son of the slave woman, I will make a nation of him also, because he is your offspring (Genesis 21:13). God's care reaches the one who is sent away.
Paul tells us: knowledge puffs up, but love builds up; anyone who loves God is known by him (1 Corinthians 8:1, 3). Knowing many things is not enough; we must build others up.

And Jesus says: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good (Matthew 5:44–45). In this Fast, let us pray for one person we find hard to love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asks us to do something very brave: to love even people who are not nice to us, and to pray for them. God makes the sun shine on everyone, good and bad. Tonight, can you pray for someone who was unkind to you? That makes you look like God's own child.

homily: Dear friends, Hagar and her son are in the wilderness, and the water is gone. She lays the boy under a bush and weeps (Genesis 21:15–16). It is one of the loneliest scenes in Scripture.

But God heard the voice of the boy; and the angel said: do not be afraid; for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is. Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water (Genesis 21:17, 19). God hears us where we are, not only when we are where we ought to be.

Jesus says: I am the good shepherd. I know my own and my own know me. I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold; so there will be one flock, one shepherd (John 10:14, 16). Today we pray for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos on the anniversary of his enthronement, that he may shepherd us with the heart of Christ.
And Paul tells us all: keep alert, stand firm in your faith, be courageous, be strong. Let all that you do be done in love (1 Corinthians 16:13–14). Amen.
kids: Children, a little boy named Ishmael was crying in the desert because he was thirsty. God heard him! And God showed his mother a well full of water. Ishmael's name means “God hears.” God hears you too, every time you pray, wherever you are. Today let us also pray for our Catholicos, the shepherd of our Church.

homily: Dear friends, Abimelech came to Abraham and said: God is with you in all that you do (Genesis 21:22). When a dispute arose over a well, Abraham did not fight; he made a covenant of peace at Beer-sheba.

Then Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God (Genesis 21:33). A tree is an act of hope. Abraham lived as a guest, trusting God's promise.

Paul reminds us that everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, provided it is received with thanksgiving (1 Timothy 4:4). We do not fast because food is evil. We fast to hunger for God, to master ourselves, and to share with the poor.
And Jesus says: I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also; for I was sent for this purpose (Luke 4:43). Let our fasting send us out to share the good news. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus did not stay in one town. He said: I must tell the good news to other towns too! Jesus wants everyone in the world to know God loves them. You can help him: tell one friend about Jesus, or invite someone to come to church with you.

homily: Dear friends, today the Book of Genesis opens its most moving chapter: after these things God tested Abraham. God called, Abraham, and he said, Here I am (Genesis 22:1). Then God asked him to offer his only son, Isaac, whom he loved.

Abraham obeyed without understanding. He laid the wood on Isaac's shoulders and carried the fire and the knife himself, and the two of them walked on together (Genesis 22:6). Isaac asked: where is the lamb? Abraham said: God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son (Genesis 22:8). The Fathers saw here Christ carrying the wood of the Cross up the hill of Calvary.

In the Gospel Jesus says that the wedding guests cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them, but the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast (Luke 5:34–35). We are in those days. We fast because our Bridegroom was taken from us to the Cross, and we fast in hope because he is risen and will return.

St Paul says: be imitators of me, as I am of Christ (1 Corinthians 11:1). Abraham's trust, Isaac's patience and Paul's example all point to Jesus. In these last weeks of the Fast, let us say each morning: Here I am, Lord. God himself will provide. Amen.
kids: Children, God asked Abraham to do something very hard, and Abraham trusted him. Isaac carried the wood up the mountain, just like Jesus carried his Cross. When Isaac asked, where is the lamb?, his father said: God will give the lamb. God gave us Jesus, the Lamb of God. Tomorrow when you wake up, say: Here I am, Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, on the mountain Abraham bound Isaac and laid him on the wood. Then the angel called: do not lay your hand on the boy; for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me (Genesis 22:12). A ram was offered in his place, and the place was named: The Lord will provide.

St Paul tells us what God provided: he who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us (Romans 8:32). Isaac came down the mountain alive; Jesus went up Calvary and gave his life, and on the third day he rose.

When Jesus spoke of his Passion, Peter tried to stop him, and Jesus said: you are setting your mind not on divine things but on human things. If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me (Mark 8:33–34).

Today we remember the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste, who stood through a winter night on a frozen lake rather than deny Christ. When one fell away, a guard took his place. Paul says: I am now rejoicing in my sufferings for your sake (Colossians 1:24). May their prayers help us carry our cross to the end of this Fast. Amen.
kids: Children, God stopped Abraham and gave a ram instead of Isaac. But God the Father gave us his own Son, Jesus, because he loves us so much. Today we remember forty brave soldiers who stood all night on ice because they loved Jesus. When something is hard this week, say: Jesus, I carry this with you.

homily: Dear friends, after Moriah Genesis gives us a list of names, and in it one small sentence: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah (Genesis 22:23). While Abraham was on the mountain, God was already preparing Isaac's future wife. God works through ordinary families.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I have compassion for the crowd, because they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat (Matthew 15:32). The disciples have only seven loaves and a few small fish.

Jesus took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds (Matthew 15:36). This is what happens at every Holy Qurbono: Christ gives, and the priest hands on what he has received.

So Paul writes: let the elders who rule well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in preaching and teaching (1 Timothy 5:17). Let us thank God for our priests, pray for them, and share our bread with the hungry. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus saw that the people were hungry and he felt sorry for them. With only seven loaves he fed thousands of people! At church the priest gives us Jesus, the Bread of Life. Tonight, say a prayer for your parish priest, and share something you like with someone else.

homily: Dear friends, today Sarah dies, and Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her (Genesis 23:2). The great man of faith is not ashamed to weep. Faith does not take away our tears; it gives them hope.

Abraham says to the Hittites: I am a stranger and an alien residing among you; give me property among you for a burying place (Genesis 23:4). He has lived for decades in the promised land, and he does not own even a grave. The patriarchs confessed that they were strangers and foreigners on the earth (Hebrews 11:13).
