Paul thanks God for the Colossians' faith and love because of the hope laid up for you in heaven (Colossians 1:5). Hope is the treasure ahead that strengthens us today.

When the Pharisees and Sadducees ask for a sign, Jesus says: no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah (Matthew 16:4). Jonah came out after three days; Christ rose on the third day. Let us pray today for our departed and walk toward Easter as pilgrims full of hope. Amen.
kids: Children, when Sarah died, Abraham cried, because he loved her. It is all right to be sad when someone we love dies. But Jesus rose from the dead on the third day, so we have hope that we will see our loved ones again with God. Tonight, pray for someone in your family who has gone to God.

homily: Dear friends, Ephron offered Abraham the field as a gift, but Abraham said: I will give the price of the field; accept it from me (Genesis 23:13). He weighed out four hundred shekels of silver according to the weights current among the merchants (Genesis 23:16). The first piece of the promised land was bought honestly and in full.

Christ paid a greater price. Paul writes: now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us (Ephesians 2:13–14).

In the boat the disciples had only one loaf, and Jesus warned them: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod (Mark 8:15). Yeast is small and hidden, and it spreads; so do hypocrisy and the hunger for power, in any heart.

Jesus asks: do you not yet understand? (Mark 8:21). The one loaf in the boat was Jesus himself. On this Friday of the Fast, as we walk the Way of the Cross, let us pay what we owe, make peace where there is a wall, and open our eyes to the Lord who gave himself for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is our peace. When people are angry, it is like building a wall between them. Jesus came to break down the walls and make us one family. If you have quarrelled with your brother, sister or a friend, say sorry today and break down the wall!

homily: Dear friends, today the field and the cave of Machpelah passed to Abraham, and Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah (Genesis 23:19). His first possession in the promised land was a grave. To bury his dead there was an act of hope.

Paul asks: then what becomes of boasting? It is excluded. For we hold that a person is justified by faith apart from works prescribed by the law (Romans 3:27–28). Abraham received the promise as a gift; so do we. And yet faith does not overthrow the law: we uphold the law (Romans 3:31).

Jesus sums up the law: this is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends (John 15:12–13). He calls us friends.

And he says: you did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last (John 15:16). Today we thank God for our four bishops ordained on this day in 2010, and we ask that each of us may bear fruit that lasts. Tomorrow the Lord opens the eyes of the blind; may he open ours. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: I call you my friends, and I chose you! Isn't that wonderful? Jesus loved us so much that he gave his life for us on the Cross. Today we pray for four of our bishops whom Jesus chose. This week, be a good friend to someone who is lonely.

homily: Dear friends, this week we follow a beautiful story in Genesis. Abraham is old, and he sends his trusted servant to find a wife for his son Isaac. The servant is worried: what if the woman will not come? Abraham says: The Lord, the God of heaven, he will send his angel before you (Genesis 24:7).
Abraham does not know how it will work out. He only knows that God has been faithful to him all his life. That is the faith we need too. We do not see the future, but we know the God who holds it.

Paul, writing from prison, asks: Pray in the Spirit at all times in every prayer and supplication (Ephesians 6:18). He calls himself an ambassador in chains. Prayer is how we keep trusting when the way is hard.

In the Gospel the leaders ask Jesus: By what authority are you doing these things? (Mark 11:28). They are not seeking the truth; they fear the crowd. In these last days of the Fast, let us come to Jesus not to argue but to obey, for his authority is the love that will lead him to the Cross. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham sent his servant on a long journey, and he told him: God will send his angel before you. When you go somewhere new, to a new class or a new place, remember: God goes ahead of you. You can say: Jesus, go before me today.

homily: Dear friends, Abraham's servant comes to a well after a long journey. Before he does anything else, he makes his camels kneel and he prays: O Lord, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today (Genesis 24:12).

He asks God for a sign: a girl who will say, Drink, and I will water your camels (Genesis 24:14). He is not looking for beauty or wealth. He is looking for a generous heart. That is the kind of heart God looks for in us too.

Paul says something surprising: I am now rejoicing in my sufferings for your sake (Colossians 1:24). Christ's Cross saved the world, but he lets us share in it. When we offer our pain with love, it becomes a gift for the whole Church. And the secret is this: Christ in you, the hope of glory (Colossians 1:27).

Jesus tells his disciples again that he will be killed and will rise. But they did not understand what he was saying and were afraid to ask him (Mark 9:32). Holy Week is coming. Let us not be afraid to ask Jesus what his Cross means for us. He will answer those who ask. Amen.
kids: Children, the servant made his camels kneel down and then he prayed. Before a test, before a game, before you say sorry to someone, you can stop and pray: Jesus, help me today. And try to be like the girl at the well: do a little more than you are asked.

homily: Dear friends, God answers prayer quickly. Before the servant had finished speaking, there was Rebekah (Genesis 24:15). He asks for a little water. She says: Drink, my lord. Then, without being asked: I will draw for your camels also, until they have finished drinking (Genesis 24:18–19).
Ten thirsty camels! She runs to the well again and again. Her generosity does not stop halfway. That is what God's love is like, and what our love should be like.

Paul says: be imitators of God, as beloved children, and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us (Ephesians 5:1–2). Christ did not give a little; he gave himself, and he gives himself still in the Holy Qurbono.

Today we remember St Patrick. He was taken as a slave to Ireland when he was a boy. He escaped, became a priest and bishop, and then went back to the same land to bring them Jesus. Like Jesus in Nazareth he brought release to the captives (Luke 4:18). May we also love even those who hurt us. Amen.
kids: Children, Rebekah gave water to a tired man, and then to all his ten camels! That is a lot of running. When Mummy asks you to help with one thing, try doing two. And remember St Patrick: he went back to the people who had made him a slave, to tell them about Jesus. That is real love.

homily: Dear friends, Abraham's servant reaches Rebekah's home. Food is set before him, but he says: I will not eat until I have told my errand (Genesis 24:33). His mission comes before his hunger. And all he talks about is his master: how God blessed Abraham and gave him a son.
That is what a true messenger does. He does not talk about himself. Jesus said the same: My food is to do the will of him who sent me (John 4:34).

Today we remember Mar Cyril of Jerusalem, a bishop who taught people preparing for baptism. He told them: the bread and wine of the Qurbono are truly the Body and Blood of the Lord; even if your eyes say otherwise, let faith make you sure (in substance). Paul says: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly (Colossians 3:16).

And Jesus says: You are the salt of the earth… You are the light of the world (Matthew 5:13–14). When the word of Christ lives in us, we become salt and light. Let us pray today for our Archbishop Thomas Mar Koorilos on his name day, and for all who teach the faith. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says you are like salt and like a lamp. Salt makes food tasty; a lamp lights up the room. When you share, tell the truth and smile at someone who is sad, you light up your home with God's love. And when you see the tabernacle in church, remember: Jesus is really there.

homily: Dear friends, today the forty days of the Great Fast are complete. Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights, and the devil came to tempt him. Long ago, in a garden full of fruit, our first parents listened to the tempter and doubted God's word (Genesis 3:1–6). In a desert without bread, Jesus answered: One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God (Matthew 4:4).

What was our fast for? Isaiah tells us: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice… to share your bread with the hungry? (Isaiah 58:6–7). David said: I will not offer burnt offerings to the Lord my God that cost me nothing (2 Samuel 24:24). And Peter reminds us what our salvation cost: not silver or gold, but the precious blood of Christ (1 Peter 1:18–19).

Today is also the feast of St Joseph, so we do not fast today. Joseph is a man of few words and quick obedience. When the angel spoke to him in a dream, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). Adam heard God's word and doubted; Joseph heard and obeyed.

The forty days end, but our journey goes on. Tomorrow we stand with Martha and Mary at the tomb of Lazarus; on Sunday we wave palms and go up to Jerusalem with the Lord. Let us ask St Joseph to walk with us as he walked with Mary and the Child. Whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord's (Romans 14:8). Amen.
kids: Children, when the devil tempted Jesus, Jesus answered with words from the Bible. You can do the same: when you feel like lying or being unkind, say a Bible word, like: Jesus, I love you more. And St Joseph, whose feast is today, did what God asked right away. Can you obey your parents right away today, like Joseph?

homily: Dear friends, the forty days ended yesterday, and tomorrow is Hosanna Sunday. Today, Lazarus Saturday, we stand at a tomb in Bethany. Mary falls at Jesus' feet and says: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (John 11:32). And Jesus began to weep (John 11:35).

Jesus is true man: he feels our grief, he cries with us. And Jesus is true God: he says, Take away the stone, and then he cries with a loud voice: Lazarus, come out! (John 11:39, 43). The dead man comes out. Jesus said to Martha: Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God? (John 11:40).

Then Jesus says to the people: Unbind him, and let him go (John 11:44). St Augustine saw here a picture of Confession: Christ gives us new life, and the Church unbinds us (in substance). Holy Week begins tomorrow. Let us come out of our tombs and be unbound in Confession before Easter.

Lazarus would die again one day. But Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who have died (1 Corinthians 15:20), and the last enemy to be destroyed is death (1 Corinthians 15:26). And like Rebekah, who was asked, Will you go with this man? and answered, I will (Genesis 24:58), let us tomorrow take our palms and say to Jesus: I will go with you. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus' friend Lazarus died, Jesus cried. Jesus cries with us when we are sad. But then he called: Lazarus, come out! and Lazarus came out alive. Jesus is stronger than death. Tomorrow bring a palm leaf to church and wave it for Jesus, our King who gives life!

homily: Dear friends, last evening Hasha Week began, the week of our Lord's Passion. Today the Gospel shows Jesus in the temple, and the chief priests and elders ask him: by what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority? (Matthew 21:23).

Jesus asks them about John's baptism, and they answer: we do not know (Matthew 21:27). They knew, but the truth would cost them. Let us be honest: we too say “I do not know” when God asks something hard of us.

Isaiah tells of a people to whom God said: this is rest; give rest to the weary; yet they would not hear (Isaiah 28:12). And Hebrews sings to the Son: they will perish, but you remain (Hebrews 1:11). The Lord who made heaven and earth stands in the temple and lets himself be questioned.

His answer will come on Friday: not a speech, but the Cross; and on Sunday, the empty tomb. This week let us go to the prayers of the hours, keep the fast, make a good confession, and give rest to someone who is weary. Amen.
kids: Children, this week is called Hasha Week. It is the most special week of the year, because Jesus suffered and died for us, and then rose again. Some people asked Jesus: who gave you the power to do these things? Jesus is God's Son. All power belongs to him, and he used it to love us. Can you say a short prayer to Jesus every evening this week?

homily: Dear friends, in today's Gospel Jesus says: now my soul is troubled (John 12:27). Our Lord is truly man. He felt fear before his Passion. He does not ask us to pretend we are never afraid.

But he also says: no, it is for this reason that I have come to this hour. Father, glorify your name (John 12:27–28). Fear is not sin. Running from God's will is the danger. Jesus gives his fear to the Father.

Moses, near death, hands the people to Joshua, and God says: be strong and bold; I will be with you (Deuteronomy 31:23). Joshua bears the same name as Jesus. Hebrews tells us that the true rest of God is still open (Hebrews 4:1), and Jesus is the one who leads us into it.

And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself (John 12:32). This week let us look at the Cross and let him draw us: make peace before Pesaha, finish our confession, and walk in the light while we have it. Amen.
kids: Children, did you know that Jesus was afraid before he died? He said: my heart is troubled. But he talked to his Father, and he was brave. When you are scared, you can do what Jesus did: tell God, and ask him to help you be brave. Jesus said that on the Cross he would pull everyone close to him. He wants you close too!

homily: Dear friends, today's Gospel is short and sad. Judas, one of the twelve, said to the chief priests: what will you give me if I betray him to you? They paid him thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:15). The Church has long remembered this on Wednesday and kept it as a day of fasting.

Judas was not a stranger. He was a friend. The greatest danger to faith often comes from inside the heart. Peter also fell; but Peter wept and came back, while Judas lost hope. Our Lord wants every fall to end in a return.

Ezekiel speaks of a sword drawn for slaughter, and then God says: return it to its sheath (Ezekiel 21:30). In Gethsemane Jesus will tell Peter to put away his sword and will drink the cup himself (John 18:11). The judgment we deserved, he takes.

He has appeared once for all at the end of the age to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself (Hebrews 9:26). That one sacrifice is made present in every Holy Qurbono. Tomorrow is Pesaha. Today let us go to confession, put away our grudges, and choose Jesus over anything the world can pay. Amen.
kids: Children, today we hear about Judas, a friend of Jesus who sold him for thirty coins. That is very sad. But Peter also did something wrong: he said he did not know Jesus. Then Peter cried and said sorry, and Jesus forgave him. If you do something wrong, do not hide from Jesus. Run back to him like Peter! Tomorrow is Pesaha, the day Jesus gave us the Holy Qurbono.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today's Gospel shows two reports leaving the empty tomb. The women run with the truth; some of the guard are paid to say: his disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep (Matthew 28:13).

St Augustine asked how sleeping witnesses could know who took the body. The truth of the Resurrection can be paid to be silent, but it cannot be paid to stay dead. The tomb was empty because the body that was crucified had been raised, glorious and alive.

St Paul tells us what this means for us: you have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead in order that we may bear fruit for God (Romans 7:4). In Baptism we died with him; now we belong to him.

This is Hevoro week, the white week, kept as one great day of Easter. Let us come to the Holy Qurbono, greet one another with Christ is risen, visit those who could not come to church, and let our lives bear fruit for God. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! On Easter morning some soldiers were paid money to tell a false story about Jesus. But nobody can stop the truth: Jesus really is alive! This whole week is Easter. Can you say to everyone at home today: Christ is risen? And they will answer: He is risen indeed!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today St Paul says: for our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed. Therefore, let us celebrate the festival (1 Corinthians 5:7–8). Easter is the true Pesaha. The Lamb was sacrificed on the Cross, and he is alive.

Before Passover, Jewish families clear every bit of leaven from the house. Paul says: clean out the old yeast, the yeast of malice and evil. A little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough (1 Corinthians 5:6). One unforgiven hurt can sour a whole family.

Jesus asks: is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket, or under the bed? (Mark 4:21). The tomb could not hide the Light. Now he has lit his light in us. We are not to hide it out of fear or shame.

And the measure you give will be the measure you get (Mark 4:24). Easter joy grows when it is shared. Let us receive the Lamb at the Holy Qurbono with clean hearts, give up one resentment, and let our light shine. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus said: nobody lights a lamp and puts it under the bed. A lamp is for shining! Jesus has put his light in your heart. You can let it shine today by being kind to someone, by telling the truth, and by saying with a big smile: Christ is risen!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today a man runs to Jesus, kneels and asks: good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life? (Mark 10:17). And Mark tells us: Jesus, looking at him, loved him (Mark 10:21).

Out of that love comes a hard call: go, sell what you own, and give the money to the poor... then come, follow me. The man went away grieving, for he had many possessions (Mark 10:21–22). Possessions are good, but they can take hold of the heart.

The disciples ask: then who can be saved? Jesus answers: for mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible (Mark 10:26–27). Four days ago we celebrated the most impossible thing of all: the Lord rose bodily from the dead. The God who did that can set our hearts free.

St Paul tells Timothy to fight the good fight, having faith and a good conscience (1 Timothy 1:18–19). This Easter week, let us give something we value to the poor, examine our conscience each night, and trust the God for whom nothing is impossible. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! A man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. Jesus looked at him with love and said: share what you have with the poor and follow me. The man went away sad because he did not want to share. But you can be different! Jesus looks at you with love too. What can you share this week with someone who has less?

intro: Theme: “Woman, you are set free.”

For eighteen years a woman had been bent over, unable to look up. Jesus sees her, calls her, lays his hands on her, and she stands straight and praises God. The evening Gospel adds the Good Samaritan: we too must stoop to lift others.

sub: She could not stand up straight for eighteen years; many carry invisible burdens for years.
Sin, grief, debt, illness, addiction can bend us so that we only look at the ground.
Like Ben Sira, we can cry to the Lord as Father in the days of trouble.
q: I cried out, “Lord, you are my Father; do not forsake me in the days of trouble, when there is no help against the proud.”
Just then there appeared a woman with a spirit that had crippled her for eighteen years. She was bent over and was quite unable to stand up straight.
points.apply: Name the burden that bends you, and bring it to Christ in prayer and confession.

points.h: Jesus sees, calls and lifts up
sub: She does not ask; Jesus sees her first and calls her.
He lays his hands on her: his touch restores dignity.
She stands upright and praises God; the Lord lifts up those who are bowed down.
q: The LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.
When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your ailment.” When he laid his hands on her, immediately she stood up straight and began praising God.
points.apply: Thank God for a time he lifted you up; tell someone about it.

sub: The Law commanded: love your neighbour as yourself.
The Samaritan saw, was moved with pity, came near, bandaged and cared.
Each of us is called to stoop and lift others, especially the forgotten.
q: You shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
points.apply: Help one person this week who is “bent over”: sick, elderly, poor or discouraged.

concl: Christ lifts up the bowed down and sends us to do the same.
This Great Fast, let him straighten us, and let us become good Samaritans.
2027-03-07.resolve: Visit or call one person who has been suffering for a long time.

intro: Theme: “I was blind, now I see.”

The Gospel of the man born blind is a journey from darkness to light, from not seeing to believing and worshipping. It is also our story: Baptism is called “illumination”, and Lent prepares us to see Christ more clearly.

sub: The disciples ask: who sinned, this man or his parents?
Jesus refuses that easy answer: God's works will be revealed in him.
Isaiah promised a day when the eyes of the blind would be opened: Christ brings that day.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned; he was born blind so that God's works might be revealed in him.”
points.apply: Never judge the suffering of others as God's punishment; offer help instead.

points.h: Go and wash: the light of Baptism
sub: Jesus makes mud, anoints the man's eyes, and sends him to the pool of Siloam, “Sent”.
He obeys, washes and comes back seeing: an image of Baptism, the sacrament of enlightenment.
Solomon prayed for an understanding mind; true sight is to see as God sees.
q: Give your servant therefore an understanding mind to govern your people, able to discern between good and evil.
“Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means Sent). Then he went and washed and came back able to see.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal faith: pray the Creed slowly each day this week.

points.h: From sight to faith and worship
sub: Questioned and expelled, the man holds to what he knows: “I was blind, now I see.”
Meeting Jesus again, he believes and worships: “Lord, I believe.”
Like Job, he moves from hearing about God to seeing him; like Bartimaeus, he follows Jesus on the way.
q: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see. … He said, “Lord, I believe.” And he worshiped him.
points.apply: Share your simple testimony with someone: what Christ has done for you.

concl: Christ is the light of the world. The real blindness is to refuse to see him.
Let us wash, believe and worship, and walk as children of light toward Easter.
2027-03-14.resolve: Spend fifteen minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, asking: “Lord, let me see.”

intro: Theme: “Hosanna to the humble King.”
Holy Week begins with palms and songs. Jesus enters Jerusalem as King, but on a donkey, and he weeps over the city. The same crowd that sings “Hosanna” will soon cry “Crucify”. Where do we stand?

sub: Zechariah foretold a king, triumphant yet humble, riding on a donkey.
Jesus does not come on a war horse; his kingdom is peace.
He wants to enter our hearts, homes and city not by force but by love.
q: Lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
So they took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord—the King of Israel!”
points.apply: Keep your blessed palm in a place of honour at home, and welcome Christ as King of your family.

sub: “Hosanna” means “Save us”: the cry of the Psalm sung by pilgrims.
Jesus weeps over the city that did not recognise the things that make for peace.
Our Hosanna must last beyond Sunday, through Good Friday.
q: Save us, we beseech you, O LORD! O LORD, we beseech you, give us success! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the LORD.
As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it, saying, “If you, even you, had only recognized on this day the things that make for peace!”
points.apply: Take part in all the services of Holy Week: Pesaha, Good Friday, Holy Saturday and Easter.

sub: Jacob foretold a ruler from Judah to whom the nations would bow.
St John sees a countless multitude from every nation, robed in white, with palms in their hands.
The palms we carry today point to the victory of the Lamb in heaven.
q: The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until tribute comes to him; and the obedience of the peoples is his.

There was a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, robed in white, with palm branches in their hands.
points.apply: Pray for persecuted Christians, who carry the palm of faithfulness today.

concl: The King enters Jerusalem to give his life. His throne will be a Cross, his crown thorns, his victory the Resurrection.
Let us follow him this week, not as a fickle crowd but as faithful disciples.
2027-03-21.resolve: Read the Passion narrative (John 18–19) with your family during Holy Week.

intro: Theme: “This is my body, given for you.”
On this holy night Jesus eats the Passover with his disciples, gives us the Holy Qurbono and the priesthood, and washes their feet. Everything we are as a Church flows from this Upper Room.

sub: In Egypt the blood of the lamb on the doorposts saved the people from death.
Jesus takes bread and the cup: his body given, his blood poured out, the new covenant.
He is the Lamb whose blood marks us in Baptism and feeds us in the Qurbono.
q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you.

Then he took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” And he did the same with the cup after supper, saying, “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood.”
points.apply: Receive Holy Communion tonight with deep faith that it is truly the Lord.

sub: Isaiah foresaw a feast for all peoples on God's mountain.
St John hears: “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”
Every Qurbono is a foretaste of that eternal banquet, and Jesus made his apostles priests to celebrate it.
q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines.
And the angel said to me, “Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”
points.apply: Pray tonight for your priests, and for vocations to the priesthood.

sub: Abraham welcomed strangers: “Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet.”
Jesus, Lord and Teacher, kneels and washes his disciples' feet.
The Eucharist and service cannot be separated: whoever receives the Lord must serve the brethren.
q: Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have set you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you.
points.apply: Do one humble service at home tonight or tomorrow, especially for someone you find difficult.

concl: Jesus loved his own to the end. In the bread and the cup he gives himself; in the basin and towel he shows how to love.
Let us receive him with faith, adore him with gratitude, and serve one another with humility.
2027-03-25.resolve: Stay with the Lord in prayer for an hour tonight, as he asked his disciples.

intro: Theme: “It is finished.”

Today we stand at the Cross with Mary and John. We do not only remember a death; we contemplate the love that saved the world. Three words guide us: he bore our sins, he cried out in our abandonment, he is the Lamb God provided.

points.h: He was wounded for our transgressions
sub: Isaiah saw the suffering Servant, crushed for our iniquities.
Jesus carries not his own sin but ours; by his wounds we are healed.
“It is finished”: not defeat but accomplishment; the work of salvation is complete.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
When Jesus had received the wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
points.apply: Look at the crucifix today and say: “Lord, you did this for me.”

sub: Jesus prays the words of Psalm 22: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
He enters even our experience of God's absence, so that no one is ever alone again.
The Psalm that begins in anguish ends in trust and praise.
q: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, from the words of my groaning?
And about three o'clock Jesus cried with a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
points.apply: Bring to the Cross someone who feels abandoned, and pray for them by name.

sub: Abraham told Isaac: “God himself will provide the lamb.”
At the Cross God provides his own Son.
A Roman centurion, seeing how Jesus died, confesses: “Truly this man was God's Son!”
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.”
Now when the centurion and those with him, who were keeping watch over Jesus, saw the earthquake and what took place, they were terrified and said, “Truly this man was God's Son!”
points.apply: Venerate the Cross with love today, and keep the fast faithfully.

concl: From the pierced side flowed blood and water: the sacraments of the Church.
Let us remain at the Cross with Mary, in silence and gratitude, waiting in hope for the third day.
2027-03-26.resolve: Keep silence and avoid entertainment from noon to three o'clock today.

intro: Theme: “The great silence of the sealed tomb.”

Holy Saturday is the day of silence. The Lord rests in the tomb; the stone is sealed and guarded. Yet the Church professes that he descended to the dead to set free the just who had gone before him (CCC 632–635). We wait, as Mary waited, in faith.

points.h: The tomb is sealed, but God is not
sub: The authorities seal the stone and post a guard, afraid of the third day.
The Psalmist trusted that God would not let his faithful one see corruption.
Human seals cannot hold the Lord of life.
q: For you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit.
So they went with the guard and made the tomb secure by sealing the stone.
points.apply: Name the “sealed tomb” in your life where you have lost hope, and entrust it to Christ.

sub: Hosea foretold: on the third day he will raise us up.
Jesus himself gave the sign: as Jonah three days in the fish, so the Son of Man in the heart of the earth.
His rest in the tomb is not the end; it is the night before the dawn.
q: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, that we may live before him.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Spend some time today in quiet waiting, without noise or screens.

points.h: Buried with him, to rise with him
sub: Ezekiel saw God opening graves and bringing his people home.
In Baptism we were buried with Christ so that we might walk in newness of life.
The grain of wheat must die to bear fruit; our dying to sin prepares Easter joy.
q: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people; and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Prepare to renew your baptismal promises at Easter: renounce sin and profess the faith.

concl: Holy Saturday teaches us to wait in faith when God seems silent.
Tomorrow the stone will be rolled away. Let us keep vigil with Mary, Mother of hope.
2027-03-27.resolve: Pray with Mary tonight: the Rosary or the Sorrowful Mysteries, waiting for the Resurrection.

intro: Theme: “He is not here; he has been raised.”

Christ is risen! This is the feast of feasts. Everything in our faith depends on it: if Christ has not been raised, our faith is futile; but Christ has been raised. Today we celebrate the victory over death, the witness of the empty tomb, and our mission to proclaim it.

sub: Isaiah promised: God will swallow up death forever and wipe away every tear.
Peter proclaims: it was impossible for death to hold him.
The Resurrection is not a return to ordinary life but the beginning of new creation.
q: He will swallow up death forever. Then the Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces.
But God raised him up, having freed him from death, because it was impossible for him to be held in its power.
points.apply: Bring your grief to the Risen Lord and let him wipe away your tears.

points.h: The empty tomb: he saw and believed
sub: Daniel came out of the lions' den unharmed because he trusted in God.
Mary Magdalene finds the stone rolled away; the beloved disciple enters, sees the linen and believes.
Faith in the Resurrection rests on the witness of those who saw the empty tomb and the risen Lord.
q: Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
Then the other disciple, who reached the tomb first, also went in, and he saw and believed.
points.apply: Profess the Creed today with special faith: “On the third day he rose again.”

sub: The angel says: “Do not be afraid”; Jesus says the same.
The women are sent to the apostles: the first announcers of Easter.
“Arise, shine”: every Christian is sent to bring Easter joy to the world.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”
points.apply: Greet your family and neighbours today with “Christ is risen!” and share the joy with someone who is sad or alone.

concl: The tomb is empty, death is defeated, and the Lord is alive.
Let us live as Easter people: without fear, full of hope, witnesses of the Risen One.
2027-03-28.resolve: During the fifty days of Easter, greet others with “Christ is risen” and pray the Glory Be with special joy.

intro: Theme: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
At the middle of the Fast: Abraham prays for the man he wronged, Jesus comes through the storm, and Peter learns to cry out.

points.h: Praying for the one we wronged
q: And the Lord restored the fortunes of Job when he had prayed for his friends; and the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.
Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The prayer of the righteous is powerful and effective.
points.apply: Pray by name each day this week for one person you have wronged.

sub: The Lord with all of you.
q: The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the Lord lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Before sleep tonight, bless each member of your family with the words of Numbers 6.

q: Save me, O God, for the waters have come up to my neck.
Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
points.apply: Make “Lord, save me” your prayer in every moment of fear or temptation this week.

concl: Fear makes us misjudge others and sink in the storm; Jesus says, it is I.
The one who cries out to him is caught by his hand.
2027-03-01.resolve: For the rest of the Fast, keep your eyes on Jesus and pray for those you have hurt.

intro: Theme: “God has brought laughter for me.”
The birth of Isaac, the children of God clothed with Christ, and the warning to the towns that saw much and did not change.

q: God is not a human being, that he should lie, or a mortal, that he should change his mind. Has he promised, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
For nothing will be impossible with God.
points.apply: Write down one promise of God from Scripture and pray it every day this week.

q: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness,
See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises quietly before the Holy Qurbono this Sunday.

q: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity that he had said he would bring upon them; and he did not do it.
From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required; and from the one to whom much has been entrusted, even more will be demanded.
points.apply: Prepare this week for a good confession, naming the graces you have wasted.

concl: God keeps his promises and turns our sorrow into laughter.
Those clothed with Christ are called to let his grace change them.
2027-03-02.resolve: Live the rest of the Fast as a child of God who does not waste grace.

intro: Theme: “So must the Son of Man be lifted up.”
At Mid-Lent the Church lifts up the Cross: the bronze serpent, the pierced one, and the God who has helped us thus far.

sub: The Son of Man lifted up.
q: Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.
points.apply: Spend five minutes each day this week looking at a crucifix in silence.

points.h: The one whom they have pierced
sub: A spirit of compassion and supplication.
Mourning as for an only child.
q: And I will pour out a spirit of compassion and supplication on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that, when they look on the one whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for an only child,
They will look on the one whom they have pierced.
points.apply: Make a good confession before the Passion Week, looking at the Cross as you examine your conscience.

points.h: Thus far the Lord has helped us
sub: The way out of every testing.
q: Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Jeshanah, and named it Ebenezer; for he said, “Thus far the Lord has helped us.”
God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength, but with the testing he will also provide the way out so that you may be able to endure it.
points.apply: Write down how God has helped you in the first half of the Fast and take up one dropped resolution again.

concl: Halfway through the Fast, the Church lifts up the Cross so that we may look and live.
The God who has helped us thus far will carry us to Golgotha and to the empty tomb.
2027-03-03.resolve: Look to the Cross every day until Easter, and finish the Fast with fresh courage.

intro: Theme: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
A family torn by jealousy, the knowledge that puffs up and the love that builds up, and the Father's generous sun.

points.h: The boy who was sent away
q: As for the son of the slave woman, I will make a nation of him also, because he is your offspring.
So it is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost.
points.apply: Reach out this week to one relative from whom your family has been divided.

q: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all offenses.
Love is patient; love is kind; love is not envious or boastful or arrogant
points.apply: Each day this week say one sincere word of encouragement to someone who is struggling.

sub: The old saying and the new command.
Sun on the evil and the good.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink;
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
points.apply: Do one concrete act of kindness this week for someone who has wronged you.

concl: God's care reaches beyond our family quarrels to the one who is sent away.
The love that prays for enemies makes us children of the Father.
2027-03-04.resolve: Pray daily for one enemy until Easter, and let love, not knowledge, rule your words.

intro: Theme: “God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.”
Ishmael in the desert, Paul's farewell, and the Good Shepherd who gathers one flock; on the anniversary of our Catholicos' enthronement.

sub: God opens her eyes to the well.
q: This poor soul cried, and was heard by the Lord, and was saved from every trouble.
Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Bring your driest place to God in prayer every day this week and ask him to open your eyes.

points.h: Stand firm, do all in love
q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
Above all, clothe yourselves with love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony.
points.apply: Choose one duty you do grudgingly and do it this week with love.

q: I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he shall feed them: he shall feed them and be their shepherd.
There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to the one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
points.apply: Pray daily for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and for Christian unity.

concl: God hears the cry of the outcast and opens eyes to hidden wells.
The Good Shepherd gathers his flock through shepherds who stand firm and do all in love.
2027-03-05.resolve: Trust that God hears you where you are, and pray every day for the shepherds of the Church.

intro: Theme: “I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also.”
Peace at the well of Beer-sheba, the true meaning of fasting, and Jesus sent to the other cities.

sub: God is with you in all that you do.
q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
but those who drink of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty. The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.
points.apply: Take one step this week to settle a dispute peacefully.

sub: We fast to hunger for God.
q: O Lord, how manifold are your works! In wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
points.apply: Pray before every meal for the rest of the Fast and give what you save to the poor.

sub: The crowds want to keep him.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
points.apply: Invite one person this week to pray with you or to come to the Holy Qurbono.

concl: Abraham made peace, planted hope and called on the Everlasting God.
Fasting with thanksgiving sends us out, like Jesus, with the good news.
2027-03-06.resolve: Fast with a thankful heart, make peace where you can, and share the good news with one person before Easter.

intro: Theme: “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.”
Abraham's test on the road to Moriah, the wood on Isaac's shoulders, and the fast of the Bridegroom's friends.

sub: Three days of walking in faith.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
By faith Abraham, when put to the test, offered up Isaac. He who had received the promises was ready to offer up his only son,
points.apply: Begin each morning this week by saying: Here I am, Lord.

sub: Father and son walk on together.
q: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him and declared, “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Look at a crucifix for a few minutes this week and thank the Father for the Lamb he provided.

points.h: When the bridegroom is taken away
sub: Why the disciples did not fast.
q: Yet even now, says the Lord, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning;
The days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days.
points.apply: Offer one hidden fast this week in memory of the Passion.

concl: Abraham trusted that God would provide; God provided his own Son.
We fast as friends of the Bridegroom, with sorrow for our sins and hope in his return.
2027-03-08.resolve: Say “Here I am” each morning and keep one hidden fast for the rest of the Great Fast.

intro: Theme: “Let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.”
The ram in Isaac's place, the Son the Father did not withhold, and the Forty Martyrs who would not turn back.

points.h: On the mount of the Lord
sub: A ram instead of his son.
The Son who was not withheld.
q: Sacrifice and offering you do not desire, but you have given me an open ear. Burnt offering and sin offering you have not required.
He who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else?
points.apply: Thank the Father tonight for one gift that came to you through the Cross.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
For this slight momentary affliction is preparing us for an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure,
points.apply: Accept one daily discomfort this week without complaint, for Christ.

sub: The guard who took the empty place.
q: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his faithful ones.
Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
points.apply: Pray this week for one Christian community that suffers for the faith.

concl: God provided the Lamb on the mountain; Christ invites us to share his Cross.
The martyrs show that no comfort is worth more than fidelity to Christ.
2027-03-09.resolve: Carry one hidden cross daily for the rest of the Fast, offered for the persecuted Church.

intro: Theme: “I have compassion for the crowd.”
God's quiet preparation in ordinary families, the honour due to those who feed us, and the Lord who takes, gives thanks, breaks and gives.

points.h: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah
sub: A list of names after Moriah.
q: For surely I know the plans I have for you, says the Lord, plans for your welfare and not for harm, to give you a future with hope.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
points.apply: Thank God this week for one ancestor through whom faith came to your family.

sub: Those who labour in preaching and teaching.
q: For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they are keeping watch over your souls and will give an account.
points.apply: Thank a priest this week and pray for him daily by name.

sub: Three days with nothing to eat.
Seven loaves and a few fish.
q: The eyes of all look to you, and you give them their food in due season.
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
points.apply: Share some of your food this week with someone in need.

concl: God prepares his future through ordinary families and feeds his people through his priests.
Christ still has compassion on the hungry crowd and gives himself as the Bread of Life.
2027-03-10.resolve: Pray daily for priests and share your bread generously for the rest of the Fast.

intro: Theme: “I am a stranger and an alien residing among you.”
Abraham's tears for Sarah, his life as a pilgrim in the land of promise, and the sign of Jonah that answers every grave.

q: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
But we do not want you to be uninformed, brothers and sisters, about those who have died, so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope.
points.apply: Pray this week by name for your departed relatives and friends.

sub: Courtesy toward the people of the land.
q: Hear my prayer, O Lord, and give ear to my cry; do not hold your peace at my tears. For I am your passing guest, an alien, like all my forebears.
All of these died in faith without having received the promises, but from a distance they saw and greeted them. They confessed that they were strangers and foreigners on the earth,
points.apply: Let go of one thing this week that ties your heart too tightly to this world.

sub: Reading the sky, missing the times.
q: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, that we may live before him.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Prepare one concrete way to celebrate the Resurrection with your family at Easter.

concl: Abraham owned nothing in the land but a grave, yet he died rich in hope.
The risen Christ is the sign that answers every death and every tear.
2027-03-11.resolve: Live the rest of the Fast as a pilgrim, praying daily for the departed.

intro: Theme: “For he is our peace.”
Abraham's honest purchase, the wall broken down by the blood of Christ, and the one Loaf in the disciples' boat.

sub: Four hundred shekels, weighed in public.
q: I will not offer burnt offerings to the Lord my God that cost me nothing.
For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body.
points.apply: Before Easter, settle one debt or set right one unfair dealing.

sub: Brought near by the blood of Christ.
q: Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the Lord; and I will heal them.
There is no longer Jew or Greek, there is no longer slave or free, there is no longer male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Make peace this week with one person from whom you are estranged.

points.h: The one loaf in the boat
q: Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, as you really are unleavened. For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
points.apply: Make the Way of the Cross this Friday and ask Christ to soften your heart.

concl: Abraham paid in silver; Christ paid in his blood to make us one household.
Honest dealings and reconciled hearts prepare us for Easter.
2027-03-12.resolve: Before Easter, settle what you owe and break down one wall of hostility.

intro: Theme: “No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends.”
A tomb in the land of promise, a faith that excludes boasting, and the Friend who chose us to bear fruit that will last.

points.h: A tomb in the land of promise
sub: The field and the cave of Machpelah.
q: For I know that my Redeemer lives, and that at the last he will stand upon the earth;
But as it is, they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God; indeed, he has prepared a city for them.
points.apply: Pray the Creed slowly this week, dwelling on the resurrection of the body.

sub: The God of Jews and Gentiles.
q: Thus says the Lord: Do not let the wise boast in their wisdom, do not let the mighty boast in their might, do not let the wealthy boast in their wealth;
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one grace you did nothing to deserve.

q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
We love because he first loved us.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for your bishop and do one hidden act of self-giving love.

concl: Abraham buried his dead in hope; Christ has opened the tomb.
Chosen as friends, we are sent to love as he loved and to bear lasting fruit.
2027-03-13.resolve: Live the last weeks of the Fast as Christ's chosen friends, humble in faith and generous in love.

intro: Theme: “Pray in the Spirit at all times.”
As the Forty Days draw to a close: the God who goes before us, the prayer that never stops, and the authority of the Son.

points.h: He will send his angel before you
sub: The God who has been faithful.
q: I am going to send an angel in front of you, to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Give one decision about the future to God each morning this week.

q: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for one priest or missionary by name.

q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
And Jesus came and said to them, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
points.apply: Bring one teaching of Jesus you find hard to him this week, not to argue but to obey.

concl: Abraham trusted the God he could not see; Paul prayed in chains.
The Son whose authority was questioned will show it on the Cross.
2027-03-15.resolve: Pray at all times in these last days of the Fast, and obey the Lord who goes before us.

intro: Theme: “Christ in you, the hope of glory.”
The prayer at the well, the sufferings that build up the Body, and the question the disciples were afraid to ask.

sub: The camels kneel; the servant prays.
q: Make me to know your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths.
If any of you is lacking in wisdom, ask God, who gives to all generously and ungrudgingly, and it will be given you.
points.apply: Pray one sentence before every important choice this week.

q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”
points.apply: Offer one daily pain this week for a named person in the Church.

sub: The second foretelling of the Passion.
q: Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things that you have not known.
Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Bring Jesus one honest question about suffering or the Cross in prayer before Hosanna Sunday.

concl: The servant prayed before he chose; Paul rejoiced to suffer for the Body.
Jesus foretold his death and rising; he waits for us to ask.
2027-03-16.resolve: Pray before every choice, offer every pain, and ask the Lord the meaning of his Cross.

intro: Theme: “Be imitators of God, as beloved children.”
On the memorial of St Patrick: Rebekah's generosity, Christ's self-offering, and the good news brought back to the land of captivity.

points.h: I will draw for your camels also
q: She opens her hand to the poor, and reaches out her hands to the needy.
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Do one small help today fully and gladly, without being asked twice.

sub: Christ gave himself up for us.
A fragrant offering on the altar.
q: Speak to all the congregation of the people of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy.
I give you a new commandment, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also should love one another.
points.apply: Give one hour of your time this week to someone who cannot repay you.

sub: Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth.
Patrick the bishop who went back.
q: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
And how are they to proclaim him unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
points.apply: Pray by name for someone who hurt you, and look for a way to do them good.

concl: Rebekah's generosity went to the end; Christ's love went to the Cross.
Patrick carried the good news back to those who had enslaved him.
2027-03-17.resolve: Live in love as Christ loved us, and bring good news even to those who have wronged us.

intro: Theme: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.”
On the memorial of Mar Cyril of Jerusalem: the faithful messenger, the catechist of the holy mysteries, and the salt and light of the world.

points.h: I will not eat until I have told my errand
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his work.
points.apply: When you speak of your faith this week, speak of what the Lord has done, not of yourself.

points.h: Let the word of Christ dwell in you
sub: Faith in the Body and Blood of the Lord.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night when he was betrayed took a loaf of bread,
points.apply: Before Easter, explain to a child or a friend what happens in the Holy Qurbono.

sub: Salt that has lost its taste.
Good works that glorify the Father.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, in which you shine like stars in the world.
points.apply: Do one good work this week quietly, so that God, not you, is praised.

concl: The servant spoke only of his master; Mar Cyril taught only Christ and his mysteries.
Faith well taught and lived becomes salt and light.
2027-03-18.resolve: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, and let your light shine for the glory of the Father.

intro: Theme: “One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.”
On the Fortieth Friday and the feast of St Joseph: the tempter overcome, the fast God chooses, and the righteous man who obeyed.

sub: Adam doubts the word in a garden of plenty.
Christ answers with the word in a desert of hunger.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin.
points.apply: Learn one verse by heart today and use it against temptation in Holy Week.

sub: An offering that costs; the precious blood.
q: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to undo the thongs of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke?

You know that you were ransomed from the futile ways inherited from your ancestors, not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without defect or blemish.
points.apply: Give what you saved in the forty days to the hungry before Sunday.

points.h: Joseph did as the angel commanded
sub: A righteous man, unwilling to shame.
q: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me; your throne shall be established forever.
When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife,
points.apply: Do at once the one thing God has long been asking of you.

concl: The forty days end in the victory of the word over the tempter.
With St Joseph we go on, obedient and hoping, toward Lazarus, Jerusalem and the Cross.
2027-03-19.resolve: Live by every word from the mouth of God, and obey it at once, like Joseph.

intro: Theme: “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”
On Lazarus Saturday: the tears of the God-man, the voice that calls the dead, the first fruits of the resurrection, and the bride who says “I will.”

sub: Lord, if you had been here.
q: he will swallow up death forever. Then the Lord God will wipe away the tears from all faces,
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live,
points.apply: Visit or call a grieving family this week and pray with them.

sub: The loud cry of the Son of God.
q: Therefore prophesy, and say to them, Thus says the Lord God: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people; and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
points.apply: Make a good Confession before Easter, and let the Church unbind you.

points.h: Will you go with this man?
sub: The thing comes from the Lord.
Do not delay me: tomorrow, Jerusalem.
q: Hear, O daughter, consider and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house,
I feel a divine jealousy for you, for I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
points.apply: Tomorrow, with your palm in your hand, tell the Lord: I will go with you through this Holy Week.

concl: The God-man weeps at the tomb and calls the dead to life; Christ is the first fruits of the resurrection.
With Rebekah we answer “I will” and go with him into Jerusalem.
2027-03-20.resolve: Come out of the tomb, be unbound, and go with Jesus into Holy Week.

intro: Theme: “But you are the same, and your years will never end.”
On Hasha Monday: the question in the temple, the rest God offers, and the Lord who remains.

q: To him was given dominion and glory and kingship, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away, and his kingship is one that shall never be destroyed.
No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it up again. I have received this command from my Father.
points.apply: Bring one truth you have been avoiding to confession before Pesaha.

sub: A garland of glory for the remnant.
q: Thus says the Lord: Stand at the crossroads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way lies; and walk in it, and find rest for your souls.
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Take one burden off a weary person during Hasha Week.

sub: The heavens wear out like clothing.
The Son who founded the earth.
He goes freely to his Passion.
q: but you are the same, and your years have no end.
I was dead, and see, I am alive forever and ever; and I have the keys of Death and of Hades.
points.apply: Each evening this week, end the day with a few minutes of silence before the cross.

concl: The Lord of all lets himself be questioned, and answers with his life.
Hasha Week asks us to stop evading and to stay with him.
2027-03-22.resolve: Keep the hours, the fast and a good confession this Hasha Week, and give rest to someone who is weary.

intro: Theme: “And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.”
On Hasha Tuesday: Moses hands on the journey, Jesus faces his hour, and the Cross draws all into God's rest.

sub: A song and a book as witness.
q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Thank God this week for someone who handed the faith on to you, and pray for whoever you must hand it on to.

sub: He does not run from his hour.
q: Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why are you disquieted within me? Hope in God; for I shall again praise him, my help and my God.
In the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverent submission.
points.apply: Tonight name one fear aloud before God and add: Father, glorify your name.

sub: The kind of death he was to die.
The rest that is still open.
q: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
So then, a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God; for those who enter God’s rest also cease from their labors as God did from his.
points.apply: Spend five minutes each day until Friday simply looking at a crucifix.

concl: The Lord who feared still chose his hour, and his Cross draws the whole world.
Jesus, the true Joshua, leads us through death into the rest of God.
2027-03-23.resolve: Make peace and finish your confession before Pesaha, and look often at the Cross this week.

intro: Theme: “He has appeared once for all at the end of the age to remove sin by the sacrifice of himself.”
On Hasha Wednesday: the sword returned to its sheath, the friend who sold his Lord, and the one sacrifice that saves.

sub: “Until he comes whose right it is.”
q: He makes wars cease to the end of the earth; he breaks the bow, and shatters the spear; he burns the shields with fire.
Put your sword back into its place; for all who take the sword will perish by the sword.
points.apply: Before Pesaha, lay down one harsh word or grudge you are keeping ready.

q: So they weighed out as my wages thirty shekels of silver.
For godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation and brings no regret, but worldly grief produces death.
points.apply: Go to confession before Pesaha, and if you fall again, come back at once.

q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
And it is by God’s will that we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
points.apply: At tomorrow's Holy Qurbono, thank Christ in silence for his one sacrifice offered for you.

concl: The Lord who was sold like a slave sets slaves free.
His one sacrifice, made present in the Holy Qurbono, is enough for every sin we bring him.
2027-03-24.resolve: Choose Jesus over every price the world offers, and come to Pesaha reconciled and confessed.

intro: Theme: “You have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead.”
On Monday of Hevoro week: the story money bought, the new belonging, and the fruit we bear for God.

sub: The truth cannot be paid to stay dead.
q: For you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit.
But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who have died.
points.apply: Greet three people this week with “Christ is risen!” and tell one why it matters to you.

points.h: Dead to the law, alive to him
sub: We belong to the risen Lord.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises quietly this week before the Holy Qurbono.

sub: Fruit for death, or fruit for God.
The new life of the Spirit.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither.
I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
points.apply: Keep one good habit begun in Lent through the whole Easter season.

concl: The tomb is empty because the crucified body was raised in glory.
In Baptism we died with Christ so that we may belong to him and bear fruit for God.
2027-03-29.resolve: Live this Hevoro week as people who belong to the risen Lord: at his altar, in honest speech, and in works of mercy.

intro: Theme: “For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.”
On Tuesday of Hevoro week: the Lamb we receive, the old yeast we clear out, and the lamp we set on the lampstand.

sub: The Lamb sacrificed on the Cross.
The Lamb given at the altar.
q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: At your next Holy Qurbono, say silently before Communion: my paschal Lamb, I thank you.

sub: A little yeast leavens the whole batch.
q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
and to clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness.
points.apply: Give up one resentment this week as your Easter offering.

sub: The tomb could not hide the Light.
Nothing hidden that will not be disclosed.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: Do one visible act of goodness tomorrow for the glory of the risen Lord.

concl: Christ our Passover has been sacrificed and is risen; the whole Christian life is his festival.
Clear out the old yeast, and let the Easter light shine.
2027-03-30.resolve: Keep the Easter festival this week with clean hearts at the altar and visible goodness in the world.

intro: Theme: “For mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible.”
On Wednesday of Hevoro week: the good fight, the look of love, and the God of the impossible.

q: The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
points.apply: Each night this week make a two-minute examination of conscience with your family.

points.h: Jesus, looking at him, loved him
sub: A man who runs and kneels.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Give something you value to someone poor this Easter week.

points.h: For God all things are possible
q: Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies also through his Spirit that dwells in you.
points.apply: Write down one thing that seems impossible in your life and give it to God at the Holy Qurbono.

concl: The Lord looks on us with love, and calls us to a freedom we cannot reach alone.
The God who raised Jesus from the dead can do in us what is impossible for us.
2027-03-31.resolve: Keep faith and a good conscience this Easter season, share what you value, and trust the God for whom all things are possible.
